# Rally-detection quality iterations — living log

**Purpose.** A running, reverse-chronological log of how we evolve rally-detection quality: each
iteration's hypothesis, what shipped, the measured (or expected) effect, and the lesson. This is the
**live** companion to the design docs — terminal-state snapshots get archived under
`docs/archives/quality-iterations/<dated>/`; this file stays at `docs/` top level and keeps growing.

**Methodology (non-negotiable).** Every quality change rides the experiment harness
([EXPERIMENT_HARNESS.md](EXPERIMENT_HARNESS.md)): new cues land **flag-gated, default OFF**; they're
graded **offline against golden labels** (per-video + LOVO-honest); promotion to default happens **only
on measured lift** through the `run_regression.py` gate; **rollback = flip a config flag, never
`git revert`.** The cues themselves are designed in [MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION_PLAN.md](MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION_PLAN.md);
scoring lives in [EVALUATION.md](EVALUATION.md); the 2-layer mental model is
[HOW_RALLY_DETECTION_WORKS.md](HOW_RALLY_DETECTION_WORKS.md).

**Golden corpus = the 6 labelled matches** in `output/human_lovo_manifest.json` (owner-confirmed
2026-06-13: use all 6 — `adarsh_avi_singles, kushagra_singles, largetest_doubles, gbaaddy,
testlarge_short, mahadevpura_singles`). The model trained on these is what we run alongside the existing
detector on NEW footage for side-by-side review.

---

## Baselines that drive strategy (IoU 0.5 vs human golden labels)

| Path | Mahadevpura (clean-ish) | Kushagra (multi-court) |
|---|---|---|
| Heuristic (velocity windowing) | 0.657 | 0.157 |
| Gen-0 owned head (LOVO, n=6) | 0.744 | 0.561 |
| Two-stage WASB+Gemini refine | 0.83 | — |
| Gemini wrapper (`gemini-flash-latest`) | 0.93 | 0.66 |

**Reading:** clean footage is commoditized (serve via Gemini); **multi-court drops the commodity wrapper
to 0.66 — that is the owned model's ship target.** Baselines tracked in `eval_baselines/`
(`heuristic_lovo_n6.json`, `gemini_wrapper_2026-06-10.json`). The owner's observed false positive — a
player **holding/flicking** the shuttle between points counted as a rally — is the precision bug the
fusion gates target.

---

## Iterations (newest first)

### I3 — Multi-signal fusion P2: the FusionSegmenter *(in progress, 2026-06-14)*
**Hypothesis.** Adjudicating shuttle-seeded windows with (a) the net-crossing **Gate A** and (b) a
person-occupancy **Gate B** raises precision on the held-shuttle / warm-up / spectator false positives,
without hurting recall (shuttle stays the primary, camera-invariant seed).
**Shipping shape.** A NEW `fusion` segmenter, **default OFF**; Gate A wired into the live trajectory path
behind `indexing.min_crossings` (default 0 = OFF → wasb/tracknet byte-identical today); court mask is an
**optional** config polygon (omit → Gate B is player-count-only; supply → masked, rejecting
spectators/adjacent courts). Person features (`players_in_court, two_sided_motion, mean_player_motion,
in_court_ratio, shuttle_player_colocation`) persisted into candidate `stats` for P3's learned fusion.
**Status.** Design via the `fusion-p2-design` workflow → implementation → adversarial review. Expected
lift to be **measured offline on the 6 golden videos via `experiment.compare(CONTROL, fusion)`**; real
held-shuttle-drop confirmation is GPU/owner-side. *(Findings appended as they land.)*

### I2 — Person cue extracted to a reusable producer (fusion P1) — [#115](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/115), 2026-06-13
Lifted the torchvision detector + ByteTrack + velocity windowing out of `yolo_hybrid` into
`backend/pipeline/detectors/person_detector.py::PersonDetector`. **No behavior change** (proven by the
unchanged `process_video` output tests); `yolo_hybrid` now orchestrates only. **Why it's a quality move:**
it makes "add the person cue to fusion" an *add-a-producer*, not a segmenter rewrite. Suite 440→441 green.

### I1 — Experiment harness: A/B without rollback risk — [#114](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/114), 2026-06-13
Shipped `backend/eval/experiment.py` — the thin variant/experiment layer (the audit's "~80% already
exists" held; pure glue over `metrics`/`calibration`/`classifier`/`training`/`regression.gt_hash`). Gives
us `Variant` (+ pinned `CONTROL`), `compare()` (labeled A/B, LOVO-honest), **`compare_unlabeled()`** (the
SxS read on NEW unlabeled footage — agreed / A-only / B-only), and a JSON experiment leaderboard. **This
is the instrument every iteration below is measured on.** 19 tests incl. the no-regression invariant
(all cues OFF ⇒ byte-identical to control). Suite 421→440 green.

### I0 — Baselines + the moat quantified (≤2026-06-10)
The Gemini battery + Gen-0 harness established the table above: clean footage commoditized (0.93);
multi-court is the wedge (wrapper 0.66 = the owned ship target; Gen-0 0.561 at only n=6). Heuristic floor
0.480, learned LOVO 0.626 (n=6). Detail: `docs/archives/quality-iterations/2026-06-multivideo-lovo/`.

---

## Standing lessons
- **Persist detection once, re-score variants forever.** The expensive/risky part is per-frame detection
  (GPU/WSL); the cheap/swappable part is the decision. Most experiments never enter the served pipeline.
- **LOVO or it didn't happen.** Score on a held-out *video*, never a held-out window from the same video
  (windows within a video are correlated and flatter the score). Sign test needs n — ~n=10/9-wins for p<0.05.
- **Small-N feature discipline.** Few, scale/translation-invariant features (counts/ratios, not raw
  coords) + a logistic regression, not a net — raw coords memorize this court/camera.
- **Gate A already existed, just wasn't wired to production** — the cheapest precision win is plumbing,
  not new capability. Always check what the eval drivers already do that the live path doesn't.

41	(Kushagra→Adarsh = 0.722). But **Kushagra is unsegmentable by *any* velocity-windowing config (0.163)** — and
42	this is NOT a WASB-recall failure: WASB tracks the shuttle **better** on Kushagra than Adarsh (**97% of GT
43	rallies contain ≥2 net-crossings**, median 5, 310 visible pts/rally, vs Adarsh 76%). The likely mechanism:
44	Kushagra's shuttle is visible 67.5% of the time (vs Adarsh 40%) — tracked *through* inter-rally activity → the
45	"shuttle-is-moving" heuristic can't place clean boundaries (mean boundary error ~5 s). **The ±0.279 spread is
46	method variance, not config.** This also **corrects the earlier "~0.73 baseline"** — that was fit-on-self; the
47	honest cross-video heuristic bar is **~0.44.**

118	## Update — n=5 + the MULTI-COURT root cause (the defining finding)
119	
120	Added **gBaaddy** (47 rallies, 1080p/60) + **TestLargeVideo** (6 rallies, 5.3K/30 — *too short to be a reliable
121	fold*). Corpus now n=5. Single-video heuristic: gBaaddy **0.277**, TestLarge 0.316 — both low. gBaaddy is 1080p/60
122	*like Adarsh* yet fails, so it's **not** a resolution/fps issue.
123	
124	### Root cause — confirmed with data (owner's insight): background games
125	WASB tracks **every** shuttle in frame, including **other courts**. Videos with background games have high shuttle
126	visibility *during the foreground game's dead time* → the velocity-windowing heuristic can't place clean boundaries.
127	The **"contrast"** metric (in-rally ÷ dead-time shuttle visibility) cleanly predicts heuristic success:
128	
129	| match | heuristic best F1 | in-rally vis | **dead-time vis** | contrast | court |
130	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
131	| Adarsh (singles) | 0.73 | 69% | 18% | **3.9×** | single |
132	| LargeTest (doubles) | 0.75 | 78% | 22% | **3.6×** | single |
133	| Mahadevpura (singles, +n=6) | 0.67 | 74% | 33% | **2.2×** | borderline (some background) |
134	| gBaaddy | 0.28 | 78% | **41%** | 1.9× | **multi (background games)** |
135	| Kushagra | 0.16 | 82% | **57%** | 1.4× | **multi (background games)** |
136	
137	The contrast metric predicts heuristic F1 **monotonically across 5 matches** (3.9×→0.73 … 1.4×→0.16) — Mahadevpura's
138	intermediate 2.2× → 0.67 lands exactly on the curve. ≥3.6× → heuristic works; ≤1.9× → fails; ~2× → borderline. **Academies are multi-court by definition**, so Kushagra/gBaaddy are the
139	**most market-representative** videos — "focus on the prominent game" is a core product requirement, not an edge case.
140	**Lever = foreground-court isolation** (spatial gate to the prominent court before windowing). The dead-time
141	detections are laterally offset (side courts), but isolation needs **real court-region detection** — a naive centroid
142	is muddied because the foreground shuttle also rests low between points. Near-term, no new model; also a *design
143	requirement* for the e2e owned model (which would learn foreground attention natively).
144	
145	### Learned prototype LOVO (n=5)
146	| held-out | per-frame AUC | learned F1 (LOVO) | oracle F1 | heuristic best |
147	|---|---|---|---|---|
148	| Adarsh (singles) | 0.879 | 0.709 | 0.722 | 0.73 |
149	| Kushagra (multi) | 0.853 | **0.561** | 0.633 | 0.16 |
150	| LargeTest (doubles) | 0.915 | 0.713 | 0.756 | 0.75 |
151	| gBaaddy (multi) | 0.833 | **0.574** | 0.574 | 0.28 |
152	| TestLarge (6 rallies) | 0.726 | 0.286 | 0.471 | 0.32 |
153	| **mean** | — | **0.568** | — | — |
154	
155	- **Recovers BOTH multi-court videos** (Kushagra 0.561, gBaaddy 0.574 vs heuristic 0.16/0.28) — the learned model's
156	  spatial-spread features (`x_std`/`y_std`) help discount background courts.
157	- **Kushagra keeps climbing with n:** 0.049 → 0.417 → **0.561**.
158	- ⚠ **Honest mean nuance:** the learned mean *dipped* 0.615 (n=3) → 0.568 (n=5) — **entirely the 6-rally TestLargeVideo
159	  fold** (F1 0.286, far too short to read). **Excluding it: 0.639** — above n=3. The mean is a blunt tool across folds
160	  ranging 6→96 rallies; the **per-video learned-vs-heuristic gap on the hard videos is the real signal**, and it's decisive.
161	
162	### Final quality metrics & conclusion (n=6)
163	**Honest cross-video LOVO mean, heuristic vs learned, by corpus size:**
164	
165	| | n=2 | n=3 | n=5 | **n=6** |
166	|---|---|---|---|---|
167	| heuristic (`calibrate_local`) | 0.443 | 0.544 | 0.463 | **0.480 ± 0.242** |
168	| learned prototype | 0.377 | 0.615 | 0.568 | **0.583** (~0.64 excl. 6-rally fold) |
169	
170	- **The learned model has led since n=3 and holds ~+0.10** (n=6: learned 0.583 vs heuristic 0.480). It stays robust as
171	  the corpus diversifies; the heuristic stays capped by the multi-court videos it can't represent (per-fold n=6: Adarsh
172	  0.751, doubles 0.737, Mahadevpura 0.657, but Kushagra **0.157** / gBaaddy **0.309**).
173	- **n=6 added MahadevpuraSingles** (borderline multi-court, contrast 2.2×): held out and trained on the *other 5*, the
174	  learned model hit **AUC 0.902 / F1 0.712** (vs heuristic 0.657) — clean generalization to an unseen match.
175	- **The decoupling is the headline:** learned held-out **AUC is 0.83–0.92 on every match *regardless of contrast***,
176	  while the heuristic swings 0.16→0.75 *with* contrast. The learned model has **decoupled from the multi-court problem**
177	  the heuristic can't escape.
178	- **The #1 near-term lever is the multi-court confound** (foreground-court isolation) — both the heuristic's biggest
179	  failure and the product's core requirement. Bottleneck = **data scale + calibration + multi-court isolation, not method.**
180	
181	## Heuristic discovery for multi-court (what we tried, what's promising)
182	
183	Motivated by the contrast finding, two label-free trajectory pre-filters were prototyped + measured at the tuned
184	operating point across all 5 videos (scripts not committed — discovery):
185	
186	| candidate | multi-court Δ (Kushagra/gBaaddy) | clean Δ (Adarsh/doubles) | verdict |
187	|---|---|---|---|
188	| **Foreground spatial gate** (keep dominant 2D-density court region) | +0.03 / +0.03 | **−0.13 / −0.12** | ❌ net −0.04 — helps multi-court a little but removes legit wide foreground points on clean videos |
189	| **Track-continuity filter** (drop implausible position jumps) | 0.00 | 0.00 | ❌ no-op — the confusion isn't transient jumps; WASB tracks a court coherently, switching at gaps |
190	
191	**Conclusion:** simple single-cue trajectory heuristics **cannot** isolate the foreground court — courts aren't
192	separable by raw density, and the learned model already handles multi-court better (AUC 0.83) by combining cues.
193	
194	**Audio for foreground discrimination — TESTED (2026-06-08), WEAK ❌.** Hypothesis: the GoPro mic sits at the
195	foreground court, so foreground hits are loud/near and background games quiet/distant → audio energy gates *"is the
196	prominent game active?"* — the signal the visual trajectory can't give. **Probed on the 2 multi-court videos + a clean
197	control** (extract audio → onset-flux + RMS energy, AUC of in-rally vs dead-time): onset/RMS AUC only **0.53–0.65**;
198	audio contrast 1.1–1.9× (below the visual contrast). High-frequency bands (8–22 kHz @ 48 kHz) raise the *contrast*
199	(Kushagra 1.1→1.7×, gBaaddy 1.3→1.9× — confirming HF-attenuates-with-distance physics) but **AUC stays ~0.6**. **Why it
200	fails:** "dead time" isn't quiet — the FOREGROUND court is loud during dead-time too (footwork, talk, shuttle pickup) +
201	gym reverb + background games, so audio loudness ≈ *court occupancy*, not *rally*. Same wall as E1 (~2.2× ceiling).
202	**Verdict: audio alone is NOT the multi-court gate.** (A learned timbre/rhythm model or audio *fused into* the learned
203	segmenter might add marginal value, but the visual learned model already hits AUC 0.85 on these videos.)
204	
205	**Court-region detection — SMOKE-TESTED (2026-06-08), LOW HEADROOM ❌.** Feasibility probe: of the DEAD-TIME shuttle
206	detections, what fraction fall OUTSIDE the foreground rally region (= separable background courts a court gate could
207	remove)? **Only 12–14% on the multi-court videos** (Kushagra 12%, gBaaddy 14%) → **86–88% of the dead-time confusion is
208	INSIDE the foreground court region.** A *perfect* court gate lifts contrast only to ~1.6–2.2× (Kushagra 1.4→1.6, gBaaddy
209	1.9→2.2) — still below the ≥3.6× "works" threshold. So the confusion is **not** spatially-separable background courts;
210	it's the **foreground court's own between-point activity** (footwork, serves, shuttle pickup) and/or background courts
211	that overlap the foreground image area. → **Court-region detection (heuristic OR a dedicated model) would NOT
212	meaningfully help.** (Doesn't need an own model — but isn't worth building either.)
213	
214	### The verdict on heuristics: it's a TEMPORAL problem, only the learned model solves it
215	Three heuristic ideas were tested this session and all came up short — **foreground spatial gate** (net −0.04),
216	**audio energy** (AUC ~0.6), **court-region separability** (12–14% out-of-region, low headroom). They fail for the SAME
217	reason: the multi-court dead-time confusion is **rally-vs-non-rally activity in the *same* place and frequency band**, not
218	a spatial or loudness difference. Distinguishing it needs the learned model's **temporal/structural** features (sustained
219	net-crossing rhythm, activity duration, spatial-spread dynamics) — which is exactly why the prototype already hits **AUC
220	0.83** on Kushagra/gBaaddy where every hand-crafted heuristic fails. **There is no cheap heuristic shortcut; the learned
221	segmenter is the path.** (A multi-feature heuristic combining cross-rate + speed + spread would just be re-deriving the
222	prototype by hand — so prefer the prototype.)
223	
224	## Learnings (carry forward)
225	- **The bottleneck is the method + data, not WASB recall or labels.** WASB delivers strong shuttle signal on both
226	  matches; the unsupervised heuristic extracts it on one and not the other. A learned model does (AUC 0.84).
227	- **Tuning is real but footage-bounded** — `merge_gap 1.0 / min_dur 2.0` transfers; the gate trades recall↔precision;
228	  velocity is ~irrelevant. But no config rescues a video the heuristic class can't represent.
229	- **Calibration, not representation, is the n=2 wall** — learned probabilities separate (AUC 0.84) but the operating
230	  point doesn't transfer across footage with one training video. **n→5 distinct matches is the highest-ROI unblock.**
231	- **Group by match, not file** for any cross-val (Adarsh-main + Adarsh-last-game = one unit; `calibrate_local` has no
232	  grouping, so keep one entry per distinct match).
233	- **Reuse the labels** — Kushagra's labels + trajectory are valuable *training data for the learned model* even though
234	  the current pipeline scores 0.16 on it. Validated empirically.
235

### Multi-signal fusion P2: the FusionSegmenter *(in progress, 2026-06-14)*
**Hypothesis.** Adjudicating shuttle-seeded windows with the net-crossing **Gate A** (`min_crossings≥2`)
and a person-occupancy **Gate B** raises **precision** on the held-shuttle / warm-up / one-sided-feed /
spectator false positives — *without* hurting recall, because the shuttle stays the primary,
camera-invariant seed.

**Scope — and an honesty boundary from the archive (read this).** The
[`2026-06-multivideo-lovo`](archives/quality-iterations/2026-06-multivideo-lovo/README.md) iteration
already smoke-tested **court-region detection as a fix for the *multi-court contrast* confound** and
found it **low-headroom**: only 12–14% of dead-time shuttle detections fall *outside* the foreground
court, so a perfect court gate lifts contrast to only ~1.6–2.2× (below the ≥3.6× "works" threshold) — the
multi-court problem is **temporal**, and the **learned model**, not a court mask, is its answer. So Gate B
here is **NOT** sold as the multi-court fix. It targets a **different, previously-untested** failure mode
(held-shuttle/warm-up/one-sided/spectator FPs). Two distinct levers; don't conflate them.

**Data support for Gate A.** The same archive shows real rallies on the multi-court matches contain
**≥2 net-crossings 97% of the time (median 5)** while a single service feed crosses ~once → `min_crossings≥2`
is a principled, data-backed discriminator (it's the held-shuttle owner-bug killer).

**Shipping shape.** A NEW `fusion` segmenter, **default OFF** (`default_segmenter` unchanged); Gate A
wired into the live trajectory path behind `indexing.min_crossings` (default 0 = OFF → wasb/tracknet
byte-identical today); the court mask is an **optional** config polygon (omit → Gate B is
player-count-only; supply → masked). Person features (`players_in_court, two_sided_motion,
mean_player_motion, in_court_ratio, shuttle_player_colocation`) persisted into candidate `stats` for P3's
learned fusion. Reuses `PersonDetector` (P1) + `rally_gate` (already existed) — no reinvention.

Completed iterations live under [`archives/quality-iterations/`](archives/quality-iterations/README.md):
- **`2026-06-initial/`** — seed of the quality phase.
- **`2026-06-human-gt-tuning/`** — first eval vs **human** GT on a partial-label video; partial-label
  harness + labeled-window methodology; baseline 0.650 → tuned 0.742 (*fit-on-self*); found+fixed a
  negative-start ingestion bug (collector PR #13).
- **`2026-06-multivideo-lovo/`** — the **n=6 corpus + honest LOVO**; established the heuristic is
  **footage-fragile** (multi-court Kushagra 0.16 / gBaaddy 0.28), the **"contrast" metric** predicts
  heuristic F1 monotonically, and a **learned per-frame prototype overtook the heuristic at n=3 and holds
  ~+0.10** (n=6: learned 0.583 vs heuristic 0.480), with **AUC 0.83–0.92 decoupled from contrast**. This
  is the data-backed green light for the owned model.

---

## Standing lessons (carry-forward)
- **Persist detection once, re-score variants forever.** Expensive/risky = per-frame detection (GPU/WSL);
  cheap/swappable = the decision. Most experiments never enter the served pipeline.
- **LOVO or it didn't happen.** Score on a held-out *video*, never a held-out window from the same video.
  Group by **match**, not file. Sign test needs n — ~n=10/9-wins for p<0.05.
- **The multi-court confound is TEMPORAL, not spatial/loudness** — three heuristics were tested and failed
  for the same reason (foreground spatial gate **−0.04**; audio energy **AUC ~0.6**; court-region
  separability **12–14% out-of-region**): the dead-time confusion is rally-vs-non-rally activity in the
  *same place and frequency band*. Only the learned model's temporal/structural features crack it (AUC
  0.83 on Kushagra/gBaaddy). **Don't re-derive these dead ends.**
- **Court-masking ≠ multi-court fix** (see above) — it's a **precision** tool for off-court persons and
  one-sided feeds, a *different* lever; measure its lift, don't assume it.
- **Net-crossings are a strong rally signal** — 97% of real rallies cross ≥2× (median 5); single feeds ~1×.
  Gate A leans on this.
- **Small-N feature discipline.** Few, scale/translation-invariant features (counts/ratios, not raw
  coords) + a logistic regression, not a net — raw coords memorize this court/camera.
- **Calibration, not representation, is the small-N wall** — learned probabilities separate (high AUC) but
  the operating point doesn't transfer with few training videos. More distinct matches is the highest-ROI
  unblock.
- **Gate A already existed, just wasn't wired to production** — the cheapest precision win is plumbing, not
  new capability. Always check what the eval drivers already do that the live path doesn't.

- **Gate A is now grounded in the archive's data**: 97% of real rallies cross the net ≥2× (median 5) vs ~1× for a single service feed → `min_crossings≥2` is principled, and it's the held-shuttle owner-bug killer.

1	"""Rally-start gate: suppress between-point false fires using shuttle net-crossings.
2	
3	WASB (shuttle-only) over-detects: when a player flicks/tosses the shuttle back to
4	the opponent for service after losing a point, that single trajectory looks like a
5	rally. The discriminator is structural, not duration-based: a real rally has the
6	shuttle crossing the net MULTIPLE times (each shot lands on the other side); a
7	single service feed crosses ~once.
8	
9	This module is camera-agnostic and needs NO new model — it works on the trajectory
10	we already produce (Frame,Visibility,X,Y). It estimates the play axis (the image
11	axis with the larger shuttle spread) and the net position (median shuttle coord on
12	that axis — the shuttle clusters at the two ends and crosses the net region often,
13	so the median sits near the net), then counts sign changes of (coord - net) across
14	the visible points inside a candidate window, with a deadband to ignore jitter.
15	
16	Gate A in the over-fire fix spectrum (B = player-stance state machine, future).
17	Pure functions only — no I/O, unit-tested; intended as a post-filter on the
18	windows from trajectory_to_action_windows, or to fold into it later.
19	"""
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	from dataclasses import dataclass
23	from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple
24	
25	Interval = Tuple[float, float]
26	
27	
28	@dataclass
29	class GatedWindow:
30	    start: float
31	    end: float
32	    crossings: int
33	    visible_points: int
34	    kept: bool
35	
36	
37	def _spread(vals: Sequence[float]) -> float:
38	    """Robust spread = p95 - p5 (ignores a few outlier detections)."""
39	    if len(vals) < 2:
40	        return 0.0
41	    s = sorted(vals)
42	    lo = s[max(0, int(0.05 * (len(s) - 1)))]
43	    hi = s[min(len(s) - 1, int(0.95 * (len(s) - 1)))]
44	    return hi - lo
45	
46	
47	def _median(vals: Sequence[float]) -> float:
48	    if not vals:
49	        return 0.0
50	    s = sorted(vals)
51	    n = len(s)
52	    return s[n // 2] if n % 2 else 0.5 * (s[n // 2 - 1] + s[n // 2])
53	
54	
55	def estimate_play_axis(points) -> Tuple[str, float, float]:
56	    """Return (axis 'x'|'y', net_value, span) from visible points.
57	
58	    Play axis = the image axis along which the shuttle travels most (larger spread).
59	    For a baseline camera that's Y (players top/bottom); for a side camera, X.
60	    """
61	    xs = [p.x for p in points if p.visible]
62	    ys = [p.y for p in points if p.visible]
63	    sx, sy = _spread(xs), _spread(ys)
64	    if sx >= sy:
65	        return "x", _median(xs), sx
66	    return "y", _median(ys), sy
67	
68	
69	def count_net_crossings(window_points, axis: str, net: float, deadband: float) -> int:
70	    """Count sign changes of (coord - net) across visible points, ignoring the
71	    deadband zone near the net (so jitter at the net doesn't inflate the count)."""
72	    crossings = 0
73	    last_side = None
74	    for p in window_points:
75	        if not p.visible:
76	            continue
77	        v = (p.x if axis == "x" else p.y) - net
78	        if abs(v) < deadband:
79	            continue
80	        side = v > 0
81	        if last_side is not None and side != last_side:
82	            crossings += 1
83	        last_side = side
84	    return crossings

87	def _points_in(points, fps: float, start: float, end: float):
88	    return [p for p in points if start * fps <= p.frame <= end * fps]
89	
90	
91	def gate_windows(points, windows: List[Interval], fps: float,
92	                 min_crossings: int = 2, deadband_frac: float = 0.06) -> List[GatedWindow]:
93	    """Annotate each (start,end) window with its shuttle net-crossing count and a
94	    keep decision (crossings >= min_crossings). Deadband is a fraction of the play
95	    axis span. Net/axis are estimated once over the whole trajectory (stable)."""
96	    axis, net, span = estimate_play_axis(points)
97	    deadband = deadband_frac * span
98	    out: List[GatedWindow] = []
99	    for (s, e) in windows:
100	        wp = _points_in(points, fps, s, e)
101	        c = count_net_crossings(wp, axis, net, deadband)
102	        vis = sum(1 for p in wp if p.visible)
103	        out.append(GatedWindow(start=s, end=e, crossings=c, visible_points=vis,
104	                               kept=c >= min_crossings))
105	    return out
106	
107	
108	def apply_gate(points, windows: List[Interval], fps: float,
109	               min_crossings: int = 2, deadband_frac: float = 0.06) -> List[Interval]:
110	    """Convenience: return only the windows that pass the crossing gate."""
111	    return [(g.start, g.end) for g in
112	            gate_windows(points, windows, fps, min_crossings, deadband_frac) if g.kept]

### 191. assistant (2026-06-13T18:59:03.453Z)

"""Pure per-window person-cue features for multi-signal rally fusion (MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION_PLAN §3.2/§4).

NO I/O, no torch, no cv2 — mirrors `rally_gate.py`'s discipline so the whole feature
math is unit-testable in a GPU-free dev container. The detection (person boxes,
shuttle trajectory) is produced elsewhere (`PersonDetector`, the WASB runner); this
module only turns those signals into a handful of **scale/translation-invariant**
features (counts / ratios / zone-membership — never raw pixel coordinates, which would
memorise this court/camera and fail to generalise off a small labelled set).

Conventions:
- A person box is ``(x1, y1, x2, y2)`` in **pixels**; ``(track_id, box)`` when motion needs it.
- ``per_frame`` is ``{frame_idx: [(track_id, box), ...]}`` keyed by the ORIGINAL video frame
  index (so it aligns directly with the shuttle trajectory's ``.frame`` — no clip re-timing).
- A shuttle point has ``.frame``, ``.visible``, ``.x``, ``.y`` (pixels) — the WASB trajectory shape.
- ``court_polygon`` is normalised 0-1 ``[(x, y), ...]`` or ``None`` (None ⇒ no mask, every
  detection counts — the player-count-only mode).
- ``net`` is ``(axis 'x'|'y', position 0-1 normalised)`` or ``None`` (None ⇒ two-sided = 0.0).

Every function degrades gracefully (returns 0.0 / empty) on missing inputs; outputs are
floats in [0, 1] except ``mean_player_motion`` (a non-negative normalised speed).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

BBox = Tuple[float, float, float, float]
Net = Tuple[str, float]


def point_in_polygon(point: Tuple[float, float], polygon: Sequence[Tuple[float, float]]) -> bool:
    """Ray-casting point-in-polygon. `point` and `polygon` share a coordinate space
    (we use normalised 0-1). Empty/degenerate polygon (<3 vertices) ⇒ False."""
    if polygon is None or len(polygon) < 3:
        return False
    x, y = point
    inside = False
    n = len(polygon)
    j = n - 1
    for i in range(n):
        xi, yi = polygon[i]
        xj, yj = polygon[j]
        # Does the horizontal ray at y cross edge (i, j)?
        if (yi > y) != (yj > y):
            x_cross = (xj - xi) * (y - yi) / (yj - yi) + xi if yj != yi else xi
            if x < x_cross:
                inside = not inside
        j = i
    return inside


def _foot_norm(box: BBox, frame_width: float, frame_height: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Normalised foot point (bottom-centre) of a person box — where the player stands,
    the right anchor for court membership. Returns (0,0) if frame dims are unusable."""
    if frame_width <= 0 or frame_height <= 0:
        return (0.0, 0.0)
    x1, _y1, x2, y2 = box
    return ((x1 + x2) / 2.0 / frame_width, y2 / frame_height)


def _center_norm(box: BBox, frame_width: float, frame_height: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    if frame_width <= 0 or frame_height <= 0:
        return (0.0, 0.0)
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = box
    return ((x1 + x2) / 2.0 / frame_width, (y1 + y2) / 2.0 / frame_height)


def person_in_court(box: BBox, frame_width: float, frame_height: float,
                    court_polygon: Optional[Sequence[Tuple[float, float]]]) -> bool:
    """Is this person on the court? Foot-point-in-polygon when a polygon is supplied;
    True (count everyone) when it is None."""
    if court_polygon is None:
        return True
    return point_in_polygon(_foot_norm(box, frame_width, frame_height), court_polygon)


def in_court_counts(per_frame: Dict[int, List[Tuple[int, BBox]]], frame_width: float,
                    frame_height: float,
                    court_polygon: Optional[Sequence[Tuple[float, float]]]) -> List[int]:
    """Per-frame count of in-court persons (one entry per sampled frame)."""
    return [
        sum(1 for _tid, box in dets if person_in_court(box, frame_width, frame_height, court_polygon))
        for _frame_idx, dets in sorted(per_frame.items())
    ]


def _median(vals: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    if not vals:
        return 0.0
    s = sorted(vals)
    n = len(s)
    return float(s[n // 2] if n % 2 else 0.5 * (s[n // 2 - 1] + s[n // 2]))


def players_in_court(counts: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Median per-frame in-court count (≈2 singles / 4 doubles; 0-1 = dead time)."""
    return _median(list(counts))


def in_court_ratio(counts: Sequence[int], min_players: int = 2) -> float:
    """Fraction of sampled frames with >= `min_players` in court (track stability vs flicker)."""
    if not counts:
        return 0.0
    return sum(1 for c in counts if c >= min_players) / len(counts)


def mean_player_motion(per_frame: Dict[int, List[Tuple[int, BBox]]],
                       frame_width: float, frame_height: float) -> float:
    """Mean per-track centre displacement between consecutive sampled frames, normalised
    by the frame width (resolution-invariant). 0.0 if <2 frames or no shared tracks."""
    if frame_width <= 0 or len(per_frame) < 2:
        return 0.0
    frames = sorted(per_frame.keys())
    steps: List[float] = []
    for a, b in zip(frames, frames[1:]):
        prev = {tid: box for tid, box in per_frame[a]}
        for tid, box in per_frame[b]:
            if tid in prev:
                cx0, cy0 = _center_norm(prev[tid], frame_width, frame_height)
                cx1, cy1 = _center_norm(box, frame_width, frame_height)
                steps.append(((cx1 - cx0) ** 2 + (cy1 - cy0) ** 2) ** 0.5)
    if not steps:
        return 0.0
    return sum(steps) / len(steps)


def two_sided_motion(per_frame: Dict[int, List[Tuple[int, BBox]]], frame_width: float,
                     frame_height: float, net: Optional[Net],
                     court_polygon: Optional[Sequence[Tuple[float, float]]]) -> float:
    """Fraction of sampled frames with >=1 in-court person on BOTH net halves.

    A real rally is two-sided; a single player feeding/holding the shuttle is one-sided.
    The net splits the play axis at `net=(axis, position)` in normalised coords. None ⇒ 0.0.
    """
    if net is None or not per_frame:
        return 0.0
    axis, pos = net
    both = 0
    for _frame_idx, dets in per_frame.items():
        near, far = False, False
        for _tid, box in dets:
            if not person_in_court(box, frame_width, frame_height, court_polygon):
                continue
            fx, fy = _foot_norm(box, frame_width, frame_height)
            coord = fx if axis == "x" else fy
            if coord < pos:
                near = True
            else:
                far = True
        if near and far:
            both += 1
    return both / len(per_frame)


def _shuttle_in_box(sx: float, sy: float, box: BBox, frame_width: float, frame_height: float,
                    pad_frac: float) -> bool:
    """Is the (pixel) shuttle point inside a person box, expanded by `pad_frac` of frame
    width/height (the 'adjacent / in-hand' tolerance)?"""
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = box
    px = pad_frac * frame_width
    py = pad_frac * frame_height
    return (x1 - px) <= sx <= (x2 + px) and (y1 - py) <= sy <= (y2 + py)


def shuttle_player_colocation(per_frame: Dict[int, List[Tuple[int, BBox]]], shuttle_points,
                              frame_width: float, frame_height: float,
                              pad_frac: float = 0.03) -> float:
    """Fraction of (visible shuttle frames that were also person-sampled) in which the
    shuttle sits inside/adjacent to a person box. **held/in-hand ⇒ high; in-flight ⇒ ~0**
    — the direct held-shuttle discriminator. 0.0 if no aligned visible shuttle frames.
    """
    if not per_frame or frame_width <= 0 or frame_height <= 0:
        return 0.0
    aligned = 0
    colocated = 0
    for p in shuttle_points or []:
        if not getattr(p, "visible", False):
            continue
        dets = per_frame.get(int(p.frame))
        if dets is None:          # shuttle frame wasn't person-sampled — can't judge
            continue
        aligned += 1
        if any(_shuttle_in_box(p.x, p.y, box, frame_width, frame_height, pad_frac)
               for _tid, box in dets):
            colocated += 1
    return colocated / aligned if aligned else 0.0


# The ~5 person features persisted into candidate `stats` (order = the learned-fusion
# feature columns appended after the shuttle features in distill_local.FEATURE_NAMES).
PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES = [
    "players_in_court", "two_sided_motion", "mean_player_motion",
    "in_court_ratio", "shuttle_player_colocation",
]


def compute_person_features(per_frame: Dict[int, List[Tuple[int, BBox]]], shuttle_points,
                            frame_width: float, frame_height: float,
                            court_polygon: Optional[Sequence[Tuple[float, float]]] = None,
                            net: Optional[Net] = None,
                            min_players: int = 2) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Aggregate the per-window person features from per-frame detections + the in-window
    shuttle trajectory. Pure; returns exactly `PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES`, all floats."""
    counts = in_court_counts(per_frame, frame_width, frame_height, court_polygon)
    return {
        "players_in_court": players_in_court(counts),
        "two_sided_motion": two_sided_motion(per_frame, frame_width, frame_height, net, court_polygon),
        "mean_player_motion": mean_player_motion(per_frame, frame_width, frame_height),
        "in_court_ratio": in_court_ratio(counts, min_players),
        "shuttle_player_colocation": shuttle_player_colocation(
            per_frame, shuttle_points, frame_width, frame_height),
    }

### 210. assistant (2026-06-13T19:03:06.587Z)

"""Multi-signal fusion segmenter (MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION_PLAN P2).

Shuttle stays PRIMARY: this reuses an existing trajectory substrate (WASB by default,
TrackNet optional) to seed candidate windows exactly as `wasb_hybrid`/`tracknet_hybrid`
do — it subclasses the same `TrajectoryHybridSegmenter` engine. It then ENRICHES each
shuttle-seeded window via two overridable seams the engine exposes:

- ``_enrich_candidate_stats`` — always adds the **net-crossing count** (Gate A signal,
  GPU-free, computed from the trajectory we already have); and, only when the person cue
  is explicitly enabled (``indexing.fusion.cue_flags.person``), the person-cue features
  (`fusion_features`), persisting them into ``candidate_segments.stats`` for the learned
  fusion (P3). The person path lazily builds ONE `PersonDetector` — so the default path
  never imports torch / touches the GPU.
- ``_select_for_handoff`` — optional served Gate A/B: when ``indexing.fusion.min_crossings``
  (and, with the person cue, ``min_players``) are raised above 0, sub-threshold windows are
  dropped from the AI handoff (the held-shuttle / one-sided-feed false-positive fix).
  **Persisted candidates remain the full superset** regardless, so the offline experiment
  harness can re-score any variant.

Defaults reproduce the substrate exactly: net_crossings/person features are persisted but
nothing is gated (thresholds 0, person OFF), so `FusionSegmenter` with default config seeds
and hands off identically to `wasb_hybrid`. Registered as ``fusion_hybrid``, NOT the default
segmenter — it is opt-in. Promotion to default happens only on measured LOVO lift through the
experiment harness (EXPERIMENT_HARNESS.md), never silently.
"""
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from backend.pipeline.segmenters.base import segmenter_registry
from backend.pipeline.segmenters.trajectory_hybrid import TrajectoryHybridSegmenter
from backend.pipeline.detectors.base import DetectorRunner
from backend.pipeline.detectors.wasb_runner import WasbRunner, WasbConfig
from backend.pipeline.detectors.tracknet_runner import TrackNetRunner, TrackNetConfig
from backend.pipeline.detectors import rally_gate
from backend.pipeline.detectors import fusion_features as ff


class FusionSegmenter(TrajectoryHybridSegmenter):
    """Shuttle trajectory (primary) + net-crossing Gate A + optional person cue (Gate B)."""

    family = "fusion"
    display_label = "Fusion"

    def __init__(self, db: Any, config: Any):
        super().__init__(db, config)
        # Built lazily only if the person cue is enabled (keeps torch/GPU off the default path).
        self._person: Optional[Any] = None

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "fusion_hybrid"

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return ("Multi-signal fusion: shuttle trajectory (WASB/TrackNet) seeds candidate rallies, "
                "net-crossing Gate A + optional person-occupancy Gate B adjudicate them, and the "
                "AI provider sets semantic boundaries.")

    def _build_runner(self, idx_cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[DetectorRunner, Dict[str, Any]]:
        substrate = idx_cfg.get("fusion", {}).get("substrate", "wasb")
        if substrate == "tracknet":
            cfg = TrackNetConfig.from_indexing_cfg(idx_cfg)
            return TrackNetRunner(cfg), {
                "weights_path": cfg.weights_path,
                "queue_length": cfg.queue_length,
                "fusion_substrate": "tracknet",
            }
        wcfg = WasbConfig.from_indexing_cfg(idx_cfg)
        return WasbRunner(wcfg), {"weights_path": wcfg.weights_path, "fusion_substrate": "wasb"}

    def _enrich_candidate_stats(self, cw: Dict[str, Any], points: List[Any], fps: float,
                                frame_width: float, video_path: str,
                                idx_cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        stats = super()._enrich_candidate_stats(cw, points, fps, frame_width, video_path, idx_cfg)
        # Gate-A signal — net-crossing count for this window. Pure, GPU-free, always persisted
        # (single service feed crosses ~once; a real rally crosses >=2x). axis/net auto-estimated
        # over the whole trajectory by rally_gate (camera-agnostic).
        gated = rally_gate.gate_windows(points, [(cw["start"], cw["end"])], fps, min_crossings=0)
        stats["net_crossings"] = float(gated[0].crossings) if gated else 0.0

        fcfg = idx_cfg.get("fusion", {})
        if fcfg.get("cue_flags", {}).get("person", False):
            stats.update(self._person_features(cw, points, fps, frame_width, video_path, fcfg))
        return stats

    def _person_features(self, cw: Dict[str, Any], points: List[Any], fps: float,
                         frame_width: float, video_path: str,
                         fcfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """GPU path (person cue ON): run the person detector over this window's ORIGINAL-video
        frame range and compute the scale/translation-invariant person features. Lazily builds
        ONE PersonDetector. ⚠ real-video verification is owner-side; this wiring is mock-tested."""
        # Lazy import so the default (person-OFF) path never pulls torch/cv2 through this module.
        from backend.pipeline.detectors.person_detector import PersonDetector
        if self._person is None:
            self._person = PersonDetector(self.config)

        frame_skip = self.config.get("indexing", {}).get("yolo_frame_skip", 3)
        start_f, end_f = int(cw["start"] * fps), int(cw["end"] * fps)
        det = self._person.detections_per_frame(video_path, start_f, end_f, frame_skip)
        fw = det["frame_width"] or frame_width
        fh = det["frame_height"] or 0.0

        poly = fcfg.get("court_polygon")
        polygon = [(float(p[0]), float(p[1])) for p in poly] if poly else None
        net = (fcfg.get("net_axis", "y"), float(fcfg.get("net_position", 0.5)))
        shuttle_in = [p for p in points if start_f <= p.frame <= end_f]
        return ff.compute_person_features(det["frames"], shuttle_in, fw, fh,
                                          court_polygon=polygon, net=net)

    def _select_for_handoff(self, windows: List[Dict[str, Any]],
                            window_stats: List[Dict[str, Any]],
                            idx_cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[int]:
        """Served Gate A/B over the (already-enriched) per-window stats. Default thresholds
        (0) keep every window → identical to the substrate. Persisted candidates are
        untouched (full superset)."""
        fcfg = idx_cfg.get("fusion", {})
        min_crossings = int(fcfg.get("min_crossings", 0))
        min_players = int(fcfg.get("min_players", 0))
        person_on = bool(fcfg.get("cue_flags", {}).get("person", False))

        keep: List[int] = []
        for i, st in enumerate(window_stats):
            if min_crossings > 0 and st.get("net_crossings", 0.0) < min_crossings:
                continue
            if person_on and min_players > 0 and st.get("players_in_court", 0.0) < min_players:
                continue
            keep.append(i)
        return keep


segmenter_registry.register(FusionSegmenter)

### 216. assistant (2026-06-13T19:04:22.616Z)

"""Pure-logic unit tests for the person-cue fusion features (backend.pipeline.detectors.fusion_features).

No GPU/torch/cv2 — synthetic person boxes + shuttle points exercise every feature path and
edge case. This is the testable core that proves the fusion math correct before any GPU run.
"""
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from backend.pipeline.detectors import fusion_features as ff


def _shuttle(frame, x, y, visible=True):
    return SimpleNamespace(frame=frame, x=x, y=y, visible=visible)


# Square unit polygon and a left-half polygon (x in [0, 0.5]).
FULL = [(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0), (0.0, 1.0)]
LEFT_HALF = [(0.0, 0.0), (0.5, 0.0), (0.5, 1.0), (0.0, 1.0)]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- point_in_polygon

def test_point_in_polygon_inside_outside():
    assert ff.point_in_polygon((0.5, 0.5), FULL) is True
    assert ff.point_in_polygon((1.5, 0.5), FULL) is False
    assert ff.point_in_polygon((0.2, 0.5), LEFT_HALF) is True
    assert ff.point_in_polygon((0.8, 0.5), LEFT_HALF) is False


def test_point_in_polygon_degenerate():
    assert ff.point_in_polygon((0.5, 0.5), None) is False
    assert ff.point_in_polygon((0.5, 0.5), [(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0)]) is False  # <3 verts


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- person_in_court

def test_person_in_court_uses_foot_point_and_polygon():
    # box foot = ((x1+x2)/2/W, y2/H). W=H=100.
    in_box = (10, 10, 30, 30)    # foot (0.2, 0.3) — left half
    out_box = (60, 10, 80, 30)   # foot (0.7, 0.3) — right half
    assert ff.person_in_court(in_box, 100, 100, LEFT_HALF) is True
    assert ff.person_in_court(out_box, 100, 100, LEFT_HALF) is False
    # None polygon => everyone counts
    assert ff.person_in_court(out_box, 100, 100, None) is True
    # Unusable frame dims => foot (0,0); with a polygon that excludes origin => False
    assert ff.person_in_court(in_box, 0, 0, LEFT_HALF) is True  # (0,0) is on left half edge-inside


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- counts / ratios

def test_in_court_counts_and_players_and_ratio():
    near = (10, 10, 30, 30)      # foot (0.2,0.3) in LEFT_HALF
    far = (60, 10, 80, 30)       # foot (0.7,0.3) NOT in LEFT_HALF
    per_frame = {0: [(1, near), (2, far)], 1: [(1, near)], 2: [], 3: [(1, near), (2, near)]}
    # With LEFT_HALF mask: counts = [1, 1, 0, 2]
    counts = ff.in_court_counts(per_frame, 100, 100, LEFT_HALF)
    assert counts == [1, 1, 0, 2]
    assert ff.players_in_court(counts) == 1.0           # median of [0,1,1,2]
    assert ff.in_court_ratio(counts, min_players=2) == pytest.approx(0.25)
    assert ff.in_court_ratio(counts, min_players=1) == pytest.approx(0.75)
    # No mask: far counts too -> [2,1,0,2]
    assert ff.in_court_counts(per_frame, 100, 100, None) == [2, 1, 0, 2]
    assert ff.players_in_court([]) == 0.0
    assert ff.in_court_ratio([]) == 0.0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- mean_player_motion

def test_mean_player_motion():
    # track 1 moves 10px in x between frames; W=H=100 -> normalized disp 0.10.
    per_frame = {0: [(1, (0, 0, 10, 10))], 1: [(1, (10, 0, 20, 10))]}
    assert ff.mean_player_motion(per_frame, 100, 100) == pytest.approx(0.10)
    # single frame -> 0; no shared track id -> 0
    assert ff.mean_player_motion({0: [(1, (0, 0, 10, 10))]}, 100, 100) == 0.0
    assert ff.mean_player_motion({0: [(1, (0, 0, 10, 10))], 1: [(2, (10, 0, 20, 10))]}, 100, 100) == 0.0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- two_sided_motion

def test_two_sided_motion():
    net = ("y", 0.5)
    near = (10, 10, 30, 40)      # foot y = 0.4 < 0.5 (near side)
    far = (10, 60, 30, 90)       # foot y = 0.9 >= 0.5 (far side)
    both = {0: [(1, near), (2, far)], 1: [(1, near)]}     # frame 0 two-sided, frame 1 one-sided
    assert ff.two_sided_motion(both, 100, 100, net, None) == pytest.approx(0.5)
    one_sided = {0: [(1, near)], 1: [(2, near)]}
    assert ff.two_sided_motion(one_sided, 100, 100, net, None) == 0.0
    assert ff.two_sided_motion(both, 100, 100, None, None) == 0.0   # no net -> 0


# ------------------------------------------------------- shuttle_player_colocation

def test_shuttle_player_colocation():
    box = (40, 40, 60, 60)
    per_frame = {0: [(1, box)], 1: [(1, box)], 2: [(1, box)]}
    # frame0 shuttle inside box (held), frame1 shuttle far (in-flight), frame2 invisible.
    shuttle = [_shuttle(0, 50, 50, True), _shuttle(1, 95, 95, True), _shuttle(2, 50, 50, False)]
    # aligned visible frames = {0, 1}; colocated = {0} -> 0.5
    assert ff.shuttle_player_colocation(per_frame, shuttle, 100, 100) == pytest.approx(0.5)
    # all-held -> 1.0
    held = [_shuttle(0, 50, 50, True), _shuttle(1, 50, 50, True)]
    assert ff.shuttle_player_colocation(per_frame, held, 100, 100) == pytest.approx(1.0)
    # no shuttle -> 0.0; shuttle frame not person-sampled -> skipped (no aligned -> 0.0)
    assert ff.shuttle_player_colocation(per_frame, [], 100, 100) == 0.0
    assert ff.shuttle_player_colocation(per_frame, [_shuttle(99, 50, 50, True)], 100, 100) == 0.0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- aggregator

def test_compute_person_features_keys():
    near = (10, 10, 30, 40)
    far = (10, 60, 30, 90)
    per_frame = {0: [(1, near), (2, far)], 1: [(1, near), (2, far)]}
    shuttle = [_shuttle(0, 20, 25, True)]
    feats = ff.compute_person_features(per_frame, shuttle, 100, 100,
                                       court_polygon=None, net=("y", 0.5))
    assert set(feats) == set(ff.PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES)
    assert all(isinstance(v, float) for v in feats.values())
    assert feats["two_sided_motion"] == pytest.approx(1.0)   # both sides occupied every frame


def test_compute_person_features_empty():
    feats = ff.compute_person_features({}, [], 100, 100)
    assert set(feats) == set(ff.PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES)
    assert all(v == 0.0 for v in feats.values())

from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from backend.pipeline.detectors.fusion_features import PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES
from backend.pipeline.segmenters.fusion_hybrid import FusionSegmenter

# Window A [1,4]s: shuttle alternates across the net every frame -> many crossings (a rally).
# Window B [10,12]s: shuttle sits at the net level (held) -> 0 crossings. fps=30.
WIN_A = {"start": 1.0, "end": 4.0, "active_frame_count": 90, "peak_velocity": 0.4,
         "mean_velocity": 0.2, "track_id_count": 2, "chunk_index": 0}
WIN_B = {"start": 10.0, "end": 12.0, "active_frame_count": 60, "peak_velocity": 0.1,
         "mean_velocity": 0.05, "track_id_count": 1, "chunk_index": 0}


def _points():
    pts = []
    for f in range(30, 120):       # window A frames: y flips 100<->900 around the net (~500)
        pts.append(SimpleNamespace(frame=f, visible=True, x=500.0, y=100.0 if f % 2 == 0 else 900.0))
    for f in range(300, 360):      # window B frames: y == net level -> deadband -> no crossings
        pts.append(SimpleNamespace(frame=f, visible=True, x=500.0, y=500.0))
    return pts


def _runner():
    r = MagicMock()
    r.healthcheck.return_value = (True, "env ok")
    r.run_predict.return_value = "out.csv"
    r.parse_trajectory_csv.return_value = _points()
    r.trajectory_to_action_windows.return_value = [dict(WIN_A), dict(WIN_B)]
    return r


def _run(indexing=None, provider_segments=None):
    provider = MagicMock()
    provider.analyze_video.return_value = (provider_segments or [{"start_time": 0.5, "end_time": 2.0}], {})
    db = MagicMock()
    db.add_candidate_segment.side_effect = [101, 102, 103, 104]
    db.add_play_segment.return_value = 200

    with patch.object(FusionSegmenter, "_build_runner", return_value=(_runner(), {"weights_path": "w"})), \
         patch.object(FusionSegmenter, "_probe_fps_width", return_value=(30.0, 1280.0)), \
         patch("backend.pipeline.segmenters.trajectory_hybrid.get_video_duration", return_value=30.0), \
         patch("backend.pipeline.segmenters.trajectory_hybrid.extract_video_chunk", return_value=True), \
         patch("backend.pipeline.segmenters.trajectory_hybrid.provider_registry") as preg, \
         patch("os.environ.get", return_value="dummy_key"):
        preg.get.return_value = provider
        seg = FusionSegmenter(db, {"indexing": indexing or {}})
        res = seg.process_video("v1", "clip.mp4")
        return db, provider, res


def _stats_calls(db):
    """Persisted stats dicts, in call order."""
    return [kw["stats"] for _a, kw in db.add_candidate_segment.call_args_list]


def test_net_crossings_persisted_and_person_off_by_default():
    db, _provider, _res = _run()
    stats = _stats_calls(db)
    assert len(stats) == 2                              # both windows persisted (superset)
    assert all("net_crossings" in s for s in stats)
    # Window A (rally) crosses many times; window B (held) zero.
    assert stats[0]["net_crossings"] >= 2
    assert stats[1]["net_crossings"] == 0.0
    # Person cue OFF by default -> NONE of the person features present.
    assert all(not any(k in s for k in PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES) for s in stats)

    assert all({"peak_velocity", "mean_velocity", "active_frame_count", "track_id_count"} <= set(s)

def test_persisted_candidates_are_superset_of_substrate_windows():
    db, _provider, _res = _run()
    spans = [(kw["start_time"], kw["end_time"]) for _a, kw in db.add_candidate_segment.call_args_list]
    assert spans == [(1.0, 4.0), (10.0, 12.0)]          # exactly the substrate windows, unfiltered


def test_default_hands_off_all_windows():

    assert provider.analyze_video.call_count == 2


def test_gate_a_drops_low_crossing_window_from_handoff_only():
    db, provider, _res = _run(indexing={"fusion": {"min_crossings": 2}})
    # Persistence is still the full superset (offline substrate intact)...
    assert len(_stats_calls(db)) == 2
    # ...but only the high-crossing window A reaches the AI handoff.
    assert provider.analyze_video.call_count == 1

### 238. assistant (2026-06-13T19:12:36.447Z)

Both ideas are sound, and the satisfying part is that they're the **same pattern at two different seams** — and one of those seams is literally the hook I just built for fusion P2. Let me lay out how I'd fit them, because doing it right is exactly what keeps this "without funky changes."

## The unifying frame

```
detectors → per-frame signals (shuttle x/y/v/vis, person boxes, net)
  │
  ├─▶ ANALYZERS  (forward, injectable, run on a window's aggregated frames)   ← idea #1
  │     emit: features + events + optional boundary hints
  ├─▶ decision  (Gate A∧B / learned classifier / AI confirm)
  │
  └─▶ RECONCILERS (backward, inconsistency-detect + correct, optional apply)  ← idea #2
        emit: issues report + corrected segments
  → scoring system / events / highlights
```

Both are **pluggable registries, default-OFF, signal-emitting, and *measured by the experiment harness before promotion*** — same discipline as the cues, so a bad idea never reaches served output and "rollback = flip a flag." That's the whole point: you keep inventing signals/fixes and let the golden-set A/B decide which survive.

## Idea #1 — injectable window analyzers (the service-fault example)

This is exactly the `RallyCue`/producer pattern `MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION_PLAN §2` sketched ("add a cue = register a producer") — your service-fault analyzer is just a concrete 3rd producer, and **the injection point already exists**: `FusionSegmenter._enrich_candidate_stats` is where per-window enrichment runs today. Generalize it from "compute fixed features" to "run each enabled analyzer over the window's aligned per-frame signals."

```python
class WindowAnalyzer(ABC):
    name: str
    def analyze(self, sig: WindowSignals) -> AnalyzerResult: ...
# WindowSignals = per-frame-aligned bundle we ALREADY produce:
#   shuttle (x,y,velocity,visible) per frame + person boxes per frame + net line + window bounds
# AnalyzerResult has up to three roles:
#   features  -> merged into candidate stats   (e.g. service_fault_prob)  → feeds classifier + harness
#   events    -> the EXISTING events table      (add_event type="service_fault", t, details)
#   boundary  -> optional deterministic rally-end (the net-halt frame)
```

Your service-fault analyzer is then ~pure logic over signals we have, no new model: scan the per-frame shuttle for *enters net region (`|coord − net| < band`, net from `rally_gate`) → velocity decays to ~0 → stays halted K frames* → emit a `net_hit` event + a `service_fault_prob` feature + a boundary hint "rally ends here." `cue_flags["service_fault"]`, default OFF.

Three design rules that keep it clean:
- **It's a *signal*, not a verdict.** The analyzer proposes; the scorer integrates. The moment an analyzer starts making final decisions you get order-dependent tangle — the thing you're trying to avoid.
- **Measure before you trust it deterministically.** Validate `service_fault_prob` as a feature/event against golden first (FP/FN on real faults); a *wrong* deterministic rally-end is worse than a soft signal. Promote to "hard boundary" only after the harness shows it's reliable.
- **It naturally feeds the eventual scoring system** — a confirmed net-hit service fault *is* a point outcome (server loses), so these events are the substrate your future umpiring/scoring layer consumes.

## Idea #2 — reconciliation pass (inconsistency detection + optional correction)

This is the **backward** counterpart: given the predicted segments + the persisted per-frame/per-window signals, find where the *decision contradicts the evidence* and propose fixes. Think of it as a **linter for rally decisions**.

```python
class ConsistencyRule(ABC):
    def check(self, segment, signals) -> Optional[Issue]:  # Issue = (kind, evidence, proposed_correction)
```
- **shuttle-inactive-but-rally** (your example): active span where shuttle visibility/velocity ≈ 0 → truncate to the last-active frame (the misfire fix).
- **no-net-crossing rally** → drop/flag (a single feed survived the gate).
- **over-merged** (long dead-time gap inside one segment) → split. **boundary-slack** → tighten to serve-contact.

Two non-negotiables make this safe and trustworthy:
- **Report-first, apply-optional.** Output an `IssuesReport` (per segment: kind, evidence, before→after, reason) *and* a corrected set. Apply under a flag or surface for human review — **never silently rewrite** (you'd lose debuggability and trust; also matches our honesty/attribution working agreement). This is the natural feeder for the v1 **correction loop** the roadmap already wants.
- **The pass is itself a `Variant` transformation → A/B-able.** "Does applying reconciliation improve LOVO F1 on the 6 golden videos?" is a one-line `experiment.compare(CONTROL, CONTROL+reconcile)`. It stays report-only until that lift is measured, then graduates to auto-apply. Idempotent + fixed rule precedence so re-running is stable.

## Where it lands (owner-gated, after fusion P2)

Fusion P2 is the **prerequisite substrate** for both: analyzers plug into its enrichment hook, reconcilers consume the per-frame/per-window signals it persists. So the sequencing is clean — P2 → analyzers (P4-style: each new cue/analyzer = register a producer) → a reconciliation stage. Each its own flag-gated PR, each measured before promotion.

## My honest take
Strong yes on both, with one caution: resist making either a *second decision layer*. Keep analyzers as signal producers and reconcilers as report-first proposers, with the scorer/harness as the single arbiter. That's what lets you pile on a dozen clever ideas (net-hit faults, let-cord, double-bounce, shuttle-out) without the pipeline becoming a pile of special cases — every one is just another column the golden set votes on.

If you want to pursue it, I'd capture this as a short `docs/ANALYZERS_AND_RECONCILERS.md` design doc (peer to `EXPERIMENT_HARNESS`/`MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION`), and I can run a design-panel workflow to pressure-test the `WindowSignals`/`AnalyzerResult`/`Issue` contracts before any code. 

Note: the **fusion-P2 adversarial review is still running** in the background — I'll fold its findings in, finish that PR (it's the substrate these build on), and log it before starting anything here. Want me to (a) draft that design doc now, (b) just keep it as captured thinking and finish P2 first, or (c) something else?

### 349. assistant (2026-06-13T19:49:27.907Z)

---
name: gotcha-shared-checkout-branch-collisions
description: Spawned tasks + sibling sessions SHARE this one git checkout (the "worktree" is NOT isolated). Branch from origin/master explicitly + re-verify HEAD before committing, or a sibling's commit gets absorbed into your squash-merge — the #116/#117 incident the owner was upset by.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

`spawn_task` tasks and sibling sessions run in the SAME working checkout as the live session here — the
"fresh worktree" is NOT isolated. They create branches and commit concurrently, so `git branch` / `git log`
can change UNDER you between two commands.

**Why (the incident, 2026-06-14 — owner explicitly upset):** while finishing fusion P2, an approved design
`spawn_task` committed `0f673ff` (the analyzers design doc) AND flipped the branch in the shared checkout in
the gap BETWEEN my `git log master..HEAD` check (which showed clean) and my `git checkout -b
feat/fusion-segmenter`. My new branch therefore started from `0f673ff`, so the **squash-merge of PR #117
silently absorbed the sibling's design doc**; PR #116 became redundant (I had to close it), and two README
index lines were dropped (needed PR #118 to fix). Messy history + wasted cleanup + an upset owner.

**How to apply — the protocol (do EVERY time, not just when suspicious):**
- **Branch from the REMOTE, explicitly:** `git fetch origin` → `git checkout -b <name> origin/master`. NEVER
  rely on the current branch being the intended base.
- **Re-verify IMMEDIATELY before `git add`/`commit`:** `git branch --show-current` AND `git log --oneline -1`
  (HEAD is yours, not a sibling's). Before opening a PR: `git log --oneline origin/master..HEAD` must show
  ONLY your commits — if it shows a sibling commit, re-cut the branch from `origin/master`.
- **Stage EXPLICIT paths** (`git add path1 path2 …`) — never `git add -A`/`.`/`-u`, so a sibling's files can't
  ride into your commit.
- **Serialize repo writes:** don't kick off a repo-writing `spawn_task`/background session while you hold
  uncommitted work — commit/push first, or wait. If one may already be running, assume the tree + current
  branch can shift, and bake the branching-safety reminder into the spawned task's prompt.

Global form added to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (applies to all projects). Ties: [[working-agreement-checkpoints]],
[[working-agreement-merging]].

1	# Global instructions (all projects)
2	
3	## Repo-freshness convention: git pull BEFORE reading
4	**Always `git pull` a repo before starting to read it** — at session start for the primary
5	working directory, and again for any sibling/local repo the moment work touches it.
6	
7	- **Why:** the owner closes every session on a "clean slate", but multiple parallel slates
8	  (sessions/machines) exist — PRs get merged and master moves between sessions, so the local
9	  checkout can silently lag the remote truth. Pull first so ramp-up reads (handoff, docs, code)
10	  reflect where the remote actually is.
11	- **How (safe form):** `git pull --ff-only` on the current branch (a plain fetch+ff). Never
12	  auto-merge, rebase, or discard local state to make a pull succeed.
13	- **If it can't fast-forward** (diverged branch, dirty tree in the way): do NOT force anything —
14	  report the state to the owner and proceed read-only on what's local, flagging that it may be
15	  stale. Uncommitted changes are often a sibling session's or the owner's WIP; never clobber them.
16	
17	## Session-handoff convention
18	Maintain a living **session handoff** for each project and use it to resume context quickly
19	across windows.
20	
21	- **Where it lives:**
22	  - If the project has an auto-memory dir (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`), keep the
23	    handoff as `session-handoff.md` there, and list it under a **"▶ Start here"** entry at the
24	    top of that project's `MEMORY.md`.
25	  - Otherwise, keep a `SESSION_HANDOFF.md` at the repo root.
26	- **What it contains** (keep it to ~1 page — it POINTS to detailed artifacts, never duplicates them):
27	  1. **You are here** — current state.
28	  2. **Next steps / open threads.**
29	  3. **Ramp-up kit** — the exact files/docs to read to get current.
30	  4. **Key decisions** — so they aren't relitigated.
31	- **At session start:** if a handoff exists, read it before starting substantive work, and use it
32	  (plus its ramp-up kit) to get up to speed instead of replaying past conversation.

### 384. assistant (2026-06-13T20:14:16.019Z)

"""Offline golden-set person-feature extractor — the fusion-P3 measurement's GPU step.

Mirrors `distill_local`'s CSV-driven flow but ADDS the ~5 person-cue features per shuttle
candidate window, by running `PersonDetector` over the ORIGINAL video. It reuses the
EXISTING golden trajectory CSVs (so **no WASB re-run**), needs **no Gemini and no DB**, and
writes one small JSON per video. The LOVO comparison (`fusion_compare.py`) then runs 100% on
CPU offline. So the GPU touches exactly one thing — person detection — and the lift is
measured by the shipped experiment harness; person features enter only as feature columns the
learned scorer weights (no special-casing, default-OFF until the golden ΔF1 justifies them).

Run (on the GPU box):
    python -m backend.eval.fusion_golden --manifest output/human_lovo_manifest.json --out-dir output

Each output `output/<name>_golden_features.json` is the replayable feature substrate — re-run
`fusion_compare` with different variants/thresholds forever without re-detecting on the GPU.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from backend.pipeline.detectors.tracknet_runner import TrackNetRunner
from backend.pipeline.detectors import rally_gate
from backend.pipeline.detectors import fusion_features as ff
from backend.eval import distill_local
from backend.eval.calibrate_wasb import load_golden_gts
from backend.eval.training import label_candidates

# The 5 fps/resolution-invariant shuttle features distill_local already computes.
SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES = list(distill_local.FEATURE_NAMES)
# The 5 person-cue features (fusion_features.PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES).
PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES = list(ff.PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES)


def _derive_video_path(spec: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Original MP4 for a manifest entry — explicit `video_path`, else derived from the
    golden labels path (``X.rallies.csv`` -> ``X.MP4``, the golden-set naming convention)."""
    if spec.get("video_path"):
        return str(spec["video_path"])
    labels = str(spec["labels"])
    if labels.endswith(".rallies.csv"):
        return labels[: -len(".rallies.csv")] + ".MP4"
    raise ValueError(f"{spec.get('name')}: no video_path and labels {labels!r} isn't *.rallies.csv")


def extract_video(spec: Dict[str, Any], detector: Optional[Any] = None,
                  frame_skip: int = 3, iou: float = 0.5) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """One golden video -> a feature record (shuttle + person features per candidate window).

    Returns ``{name, fps, frame_width, candidates:[{start,end,shuttle{},person{},label}], gts}``.
    `detector` (anything with ``detections_per_frame``) is injectable for GPU-free tests; when
    None a real `PersonDetector` is built (loads torchvision on first use).
    """
    fps, fw = float(spec["fps"]), float(spec["frame_width"])
    traj = str(spec["trajectory"])
    points = TrackNetRunner.parse_trajectory_csv(traj)
    intervals, x_shuttle = distill_local.build_candidates(traj, fps, fw)
    gts = load_golden_gts(str(spec["labels"]))
    labels = label_candidates(intervals, gts, iou)
    # Net axis for the person two-sided split — reuse rally_gate's camera-agnostic estimate
    # (parity with the shuttle net-crossing gate) rather than hard-coding an orientation.
    axis, net_px, _span = rally_gate.estimate_play_axis(points)
    video_path = _derive_video_path(spec)

    if detector is None:
        from backend.pipeline.detectors.person_detector import PersonDetector
        detector = PersonDetector({"indexing": {"use_gpu": True}})

    candidates: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for i, ((s, e), xs) in enumerate(zip(intervals, x_shuttle)):
        sf, ef = round(s * fps), round(e * fps)
        det = detector.detections_per_frame(video_path, sf, ef, frame_skip)
        det_fw = det.get("frame_width") or fw
        det_fh = det.get("frame_height") or 0.0
        # Normalise the (pixel) net coord to 0-1 on the play axis, matching the foot-point
        # normalisation fusion_features uses (x/width, y/height).
        if axis == "x":
            net_norm = net_px / det_fw if det_fw > 0 else 0.5
        else:
            net_norm = net_px / det_fh if det_fh > 0 else 0.5
        shuttle_in = [p for p in points if sf <= p.frame <= ef]
        person = ff.compute_person_features(det["frames"], shuttle_in, det_fw, det_fh,
                                            court_polygon=None, net=(axis, net_norm))
        candidates.append({
            "start": float(s), "end": float(e),
            "shuttle": {k: float(v) for k, v in zip(SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES, xs)},
            "person": {k: float(v) for k, v in person.items()},
            "label": int(labels[i]),
        })
    return {
        "name": spec["name"], "fps": fps, "frame_width": fw,
        "candidates": candidates,
        "gts": [[float(a), float(b)] for a, b in gts],
    }


def run(manifest_path: str, out_dir: str, frame_skip: int = 3, iou: float = 0.5) -> List[str]:
    with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        specs = json.load(f)
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    written: List[str] = []
    for spec in specs:
        print(f"[fusion_golden] {spec['name']}: extracting shuttle+person features...", flush=True)
        data = extract_video(spec, frame_skip=frame_skip, iou=iou)
        n_pos = sum(c["label"] for c in data["candidates"])
        print(f"[fusion_golden] {spec['name']}: {len(data['candidates'])} windows "
              f"({n_pos} positive) | {len(data['gts'])} golden rallies", flush=True)
        out = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{spec['name']}_golden_features.json")
        with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
        print(f"[fusion_golden] -> {out}", flush=True)
        written.append(out)
    return written


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Extract golden-set shuttle+person features (fusion P3 GPU step).")
    ap.add_argument("--manifest", default="output/human_lovo_manifest.json")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="output")
    ap.add_argument("--frame-skip", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--iou", type=float, default=0.5)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    run(args.manifest, args.out_dir, args.frame_skip, args.iou)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

### 386. assistant (2026-06-13T20:14:36.147Z)

"""Pure-CPU LOVO comparison: shuttle-only vs shuttle+person learned fusion on the golden set.

The fusion-P3 measurement. Loads the per-video feature JSONs written by `fusion_golden.py`
and runs the SHIPPED experiment harness (`experiment.compare`, honest leave-one-video-out) —
no new scoring/labeling math. The two variants differ ONLY by `feature_names` (the harness's
designed seam): the person features are extra columns the learned LogisticRegression weights,
so the held-out ΔF1 is an honest answer to "does the person cue help?" — not a hunch.

Run (no GPU):
    python -m backend.eval.fusion_compare --features-dir output --record
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from backend.eval import experiment
from backend.eval.fusion_golden import PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES, SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES


def load_videos(features_dir: str) -> List[experiment.VideoCandidates]:
    """Load every ``*_golden_features.json`` into a VideoCandidates (intervals + the 10
    feature columns + golden gts). The harness derives labels from gts itself."""
    videos: List[experiment.VideoCandidates] = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(features_dir, "*_golden_features.json"))):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            d = json.load(f)
        cands = d["candidates"]
        intervals = [(float(c["start"]), float(c["end"])) for c in cands]
        features: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
        for fn in SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES:
            features[fn] = [float(c["shuttle"][fn]) for c in cands]
        for fn in PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES:
            features[fn] = [float(c["person"][fn]) for c in cands]
        gts = [(float(a), float(b)) for a, b in d["gts"]]
        videos.append(experiment.VideoCandidates(name=d["name"], intervals=intervals,
                                                 features=features, gts=gts))
    return videos


def compare(videos: List[experiment.VideoCandidates], iou: float = 0.5,
            threshold: float = 0.5) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    shuttle_only = experiment.Variant(name="shuttle_only", feature_names=list(SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES),
                                      threshold=threshold)
    fusion = experiment.Variant(name="shuttle_person_fusion",
                                feature_names=list(SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES) + list(PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES),
                                threshold=threshold)
    return experiment.compare(videos, shuttle_only, fusion, iou=iou, honest=True)


def format_result(res: Dict[str, Any], iou: float) -> str:
    a, b, d = res["variant_a"]["aggregate"], res["variant_b"]["aggregate"], res["delta"]
    lines = [
        f"=== Fusion P3 LOVO (n={res['num_videos']} golden videos, IoU>={iou}, honest) ===",
        f"  shuttle-only : F1={a['f1']:.3f}  P={a['precision']:.3f}  R={a['recall']:.3f}  IoU={a['mean_iou']:.3f}",
        f"  +person      : F1={b['f1']:.3f}  P={b['precision']:.3f}  R={b['recall']:.3f}  IoU={b['mean_iou']:.3f}",
        f"  ΔF1 = {d['f1']:+.3f}  ({res['delta_pct']['f1']:+.1f}%)   ΔP={d['precision']:+.3f}  ΔR={d['recall']:+.3f}",
        "  per-video ΔF1:",
    ]
    for pv in res["per_video_delta"]:
        lines.append(f"    {pv['video']:<26s} ΔF1={pv['f1']:+.3f}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LOVO fusion lift: shuttle-only vs shuttle+person (golden set).")
    ap.add_argument("--features-dir", default="output")
    ap.add_argument("--iou", type=float, default=0.5)
    ap.add_argument("--record", action="store_true", help="append the result to the experiment leaderboard")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    videos = load_videos(args.features_dir)
    if len(videos) < 2:
        raise SystemExit(f"need >=2 *_golden_features.json in {args.features_dir} (found {len(videos)})")
    res = compare(videos, iou=args.iou)
    print(format_result(res, args.iou))
    if args.record:
        row = experiment.record_experiment(res)
        print(f"recorded -> eval_baselines/experiment_leaderboard.json ({row['timestamp']})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

### 389. assistant (2026-06-13T20:15:24.329Z)

"""GPU-free tests for the fusion-P3 measurement (fusion_golden extractor + fusion_compare LOVO).

The LOVO driver is exercised on a synthetic 6-video set where the SHUTTLE features are
non-separating (constant) but a PERSON feature cleanly separates rallies — so the harness must
report a positive fusion ΔF1. The extractor is exercised with a stubbed detector (no GPU).
"""
import json
import os
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from backend.eval import fusion_compare
from backend.eval.fusion_compare import PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES, SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES


def _write_video(d, name):
    """A video whose shuttle features are identical for pos/neg (no signal) but whose
    players_in_court separates rallies (4) from junk (0)."""
    cands = []
    for (s, e), pos in [((0.0, 10.0), 1), ((20.0, 30.0), 1), ((40.0, 41.0), 0), ((50.0, 51.0), 0)]:
        shuttle = {fn: 1.0 for fn in SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES}                 # constant -> non-separating
        person = {fn: 0.0 for fn in PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES}
        person["players_in_court"] = 4.0 if pos else 0.0                   # the separating signal
        person["in_court_ratio"] = 1.0 if pos else 0.0
        cands.append({"start": s, "end": e, "shuttle": shuttle, "person": person, "label": pos})
    data = {"name": name, "fps": 30.0, "frame_width": 1920.0,
            "candidates": cands, "gts": [[0.0, 10.0], [20.0, 30.0]]}
    with open(os.path.join(d, f"{name}_golden_features.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f)


def test_fusion_compare_reports_person_driven_lift(tmp_path):
    d = str(tmp_path)
    for k in range(6):
        _write_video(d, f"vid{k}")
    videos = fusion_compare.load_videos(d)
    assert len(videos) == 6
    res = fusion_compare.compare(videos, iou=0.5)
    assert res["num_videos"] == 6
    assert res["variant_b"]["honest_lovo"] is True                 # LOVO-honest learned variant
    # Fusion (with the separating person feature) must beat shuttle-only (no signal).
    assert res["delta"]["f1"] > 0.0
    assert res["variant_b"]["aggregate"]["f1"] > res["variant_a"]["aggregate"]["f1"]
    # format_result must not crash and must mention both variants.
    out = fusion_compare.format_result(res, 0.5)
    assert "shuttle-only" in out and "+person" in out


def test_fusion_compare_needs_two_videos(tmp_path):
    _write_video(str(tmp_path), "only")
    videos = fusion_compare.load_videos(str(tmp_path))
    assert len(videos) == 1  # compare() / experiment.compare needs >=2 for honest LOVO


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- extractor assembly

def test_extract_video_assembles_shuttle_and_person(monkeypatch):
    from backend.eval import fusion_golden
    from backend.pipeline.detectors.tracknet_runner import TrackNetRunner

    intervals = [(0.0, 10.0), (40.0, 41.0)]
    x_shuttle = [[10.0, 0.3, 0.2, 0.5, 4.0], [1.0, 0.1, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0]]
    points = [SimpleNamespace(frame=i, visible=True, x=500.0, y=(100.0 if i % 2 else 900.0))
              for i in range(10)]

    monkeypatch.setattr(fusion_golden.distill_local, "build_candidates",
                        lambda traj, fps, fw: (intervals, x_shuttle))
    monkeypatch.setattr(TrackNetRunner, "parse_trajectory_csv", staticmethod(lambda traj: points))
    monkeypatch.setattr(fusion_golden, "load_golden_gts", lambda labels: [(0.0, 10.0)])

    class _StubDetector:
        def detections_per_frame(self, video, sf, ef, frame_skip):
            return {"frames": {sf: [(1, (10.0, 10.0, 30.0, 40.0))]},
                    "frame_width": 1920.0, "frame_height": 1080.0}

    spec = {"name": "t", "trajectory": "bar.csv", "fps": 30.0, "frame_width": 1920.0,
            "labels": "foo.rallies.csv"}
    data = fusion_golden.extract_video(spec, detector=_StubDetector(), frame_skip=3, iou=0.5)

    assert data["name"] == "t"
    assert data["gts"] == [[0.0, 10.0]]
    assert len(data["candidates"]) == 2
    c0 = data["candidates"][0]
    assert set(c0["shuttle"]) == set(SHUTTLE_FEATURE_NAMES)
    assert set(c0["person"]) == set(PERSON_FEATURE_NAMES)
    assert c0["label"] == 1                     # (0,10) matches the gt -> positive
    assert data["candidates"][1]["label"] == 0  # (40,41) -> negative
    assert all(isinstance(v, float) for v in c0["person"].values())


def test_derive_video_path():
    from backend.eval.fusion_golden import _derive_video_path
    assert _derive_video_path({"labels": "X/Adarsh and Avi.rallies.csv"}) == "X/Adarsh and Avi.MP4"
    assert _derive_video_path({"video_path": "a.mp4", "labels": "b.rallies.csv"}) == "a.mp4"
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _derive_video_path({"name": "n", "labels": "weird.csv"})
