### 966. assistant (2026-06-14T08:24:32.847Z)

Both launched. While they run, here's my **initial read** (the rigorous version with web grounding + a strict counter-case is coming as a written proposal):

**Why this pivot is architecturally natural — not a rewrite:** the whole stack you've built is *already a per-corpus optimizer*. LOVO + A/B + promote-only-on-lift + default-OFF signals-as-feature-columns + the correction loop = a machine that decides "which signals earn their keep on *this* set of videos." A **per-user corpus is just a special case of that corpus.** So "motion cue off for this user" isn't new code — it's a per-user `Variant` decision the harness already makes. That's the strongest pro: the moat you've invested in (honest measurement) *is* the personalization engine.

**The core trade I see:**

| | Personalization-first | Generalization-first |
|---|---|---|
| **Moat** | Per-user tuned model + their corpus = sticky, hard to copy | One model; easier to commoditize |
| **Privacy** | On-device, data never leaves — a *selling point* | Cloud corpus; consent/GDPR overhead |
| **Data licensing** | User's own video = commercial-clean, no 3rd-party copyright | Needs a clean pooled corpus |
| **Cold-start** | Weak until ~5–15 videos (the "batteries" must carry it) | Strong day-one if the corpus is broad |
| **Eval honesty** | Per-user N is *even smaller* than n=6 → promotion noise is the central risk | Bigger corpus, cleaner stats |
| **Shot taxonomy** | Serves/smashes/drives need per-user labels → hardest cold-start | Same, but amortized across users |

**The two things I'll be watching the research resolve:** (1) the **small-N-per-user eval-noise** problem — your own n=6 lesson says per-user A/B could promote noise, so the batteries baseline + a conservative per-user gate matter enormously; (2) **what actually personalizes on-device** — almost certainly the *lightweight learned head + cue selection* on the frozen WASB substrate, **not** on-device fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL (infeasible on a hobbyist's machine). That single distinction reshapes the owned-model roadmap.

When the workflow lands I'll deliver the full **`scratch/PERSONALIZATION_PIVOT_ANALYSIS.md`** — pros/cons, harness-fit + gap list, what it changes about owned-model/data/product/business, risks + mitigations, a recommendation, and the **decision points it forces you to make**. ### 997. assistant (2026-06-14T08:58:26.525Z)

# Personalization Feature — Implementation Design & Phased Build Plan

> **Status: DESIGN — owner-review-gated.** The hybrid the owner adopted: a generalization-first
> baseline + a flag-gated per-user personalization *feature* + a **contribution flywheel**.
> Foundation principle: *"a tool that gets better the more you help it"* — contribution
> (data / video / diagnostics / annotation) improves BOTH the user's own model AND the shared
> baseline; **payoff scales with contribution**. Companion to `scratch/PERSONALIZATION_PIVOT_ANALYSIS.md`.

## Executive summary
The hybrid is buildable on the existing harness because the codebase already cleanly separates
**expensive detection** (persisted once into `candidate_segments.stats`) from **cheap, swappable
decision** (offline re-scoring via `experiment.Variant`). Personalization = per-user re-scoring of
already-persisted features. The four real walls, all verified in code:
1. `LogisticRegression.load` is **never called** in `backend/pipeline/` — the served seam
   (`fusion_hybrid._select_for_handoff`) reads only Gate thresholds, so a learned per-user model has
   **no serving path** (the #1 wall).
2. `human_label` is a **read-only stub** (column + `only_unlabeled` filter, no setter/API) —
   corrections can't become labels.
3. There is **no user/tenant dimension** anywhere.
4. The validated day-0 win (label-free Gate-A/B fusion, ΔF1 +0.074, 6/6, p=0.031) is opt-in but
   not shipped as the default battery.

Every per-user promotion rides the existing honest small-N bar (`eval_stats.paired_delta_ci` + sign
test) with a **hard min-N floor**, falling back to the baseline below it. The headline "<5 videos to
superior quality" becomes a **falsifiable held-out-USER release criterion**, not a slogan.

## Architecture
**Two-layer decoupling (already real).** Detection layer (GPU, run once): `FusionSegmenter` persists
the **full superset** of per-window features into `candidate_segments.stats`; only the served handoff
is gated. Decision layer (CPU, swappable): `experiment.Variant` + `predict()` re-score persisted
features. **Personalization == a per-user `Variant`** (cue_flags + min_crossings/min_players + optional
LogReg + threshold).

**The single highest-leverage wiring:** `fusion_hybrid.py::_select_for_handoff` is the exact
production decision seam. A new **per-user `FusionConfig` overlay** resolves there; when a per-user
model is pinned AND the promotion gate says ON, apply `LogisticRegression.predict_proba` over
`window_stats` (same math `experiment.predict()` runs offline). Persisted candidates stay the full
superset (invariant unchanged); default path (no `user_id`) untouched.

## Per-user data model (migrations follow the `PRAGMA user_version` ladder; current = v3)
- **v4 — tenant dimension:** nullable `user_id` on `videos` + `candidate_segments` (+ indexes).
  `user_id IS NULL` = legacy/local single-user → byte-identical to today.
- **v5 — `user_models` store:** `(user_id, version, baseline_version, feature_schema_hash,
  fusion_config JSON, classifier_json, promotion_evidence, n_videos_at_fit, is_active)`. Inline
  `classifier_json` (tenant-safe, self-contained; `LogisticRegression.from_dict` round-trips).
  `feature_schema_hash` = the MINOR-vs-MAJOR upgrade switch (MAJOR e.g. the M0.4 ActionFormer swap
  invalidates the 5-feature LogReg → re-fit from stored correction labels).
- **v6 — consent ledger:** `contribution_consent(user_id, scope, granted, is_minor_attested, ...)`,
  default-deny, **enforced at the pooling query** (`WHERE granted=1 AND is_minor_attested=0`).

## Serving bridge (closes wall #1) — `backend/pipeline/personalization/serving.py`
- `resolve_user_fusion_config(db, user_id, served_cfg)` — overlay the active `user_models` row onto
  `served_cfg["fusion"]`; if no active model or `n_videos_at_fit < min_n`, return the **shipped
  baseline** (cold-start fallback = Gate-A/B day-0 battery).
- `load_user_classifier(db, user_id)` — `LogisticRegression.from_dict(...)`. **First production caller
  of the load path.** Wired into `_select_for_handoff` after the Gate-A/B mask.

## APIs (`backend/main.py`, reuse the async job model)
- `POST /api/candidates/{id}/label` — sets `human_label` (confirm|reject) — **first production writer**.
- `POST /api/users/{user_id}/retune` — 202 job: per-user LOVO over the grown corpus → fit/refresh the
  `user_models` row → per-user no-regression guard → activate only if it passes.
- `GET /api/users/{user_id}/model` — the **trust feature**: per-cue ON/OFF + promotion evidence
  ("we tested motion on YOUR videos — it didn't help, so it's off").
- `POST /api/users/{user_id}/consent` — consent ledger write (scope + minor attestation).
- `GET /api/users/{user_id}/annotation-task` — active-learning ~2-min high-uncertainty segment.

## Constructs → real code
1. **Per-user store + serving bridge** — v4/v5 + `serving.py` + the `_select_for_handoff` wiring.
2. **Correction-loop → labels** — the `POST .../label` setter + `db.set_human_label(...)` +
   a **recall-protecting de-bias prior** (corrections are FP-biased; `class_weight="balanced"` is the
   hook, add a miss-inflation factor) + active-learning surfacing of high-uncertainty *unfired* windows.
3. **Per-user promotion gate** — **already built** (`per_user_gate.py`, PR #141): min-N floor +
   structural-guard exemption; surface `PromotionDecision.as_dict()` as the trust feature.
4. **Contribution flywheel** — consent ledger + opt-in upload (reuse chunked upload, per-user scoped).
   **Payoff-scales:** a multi-video user with reproduced capture settings gets a fit `user_models`
   row; a single-video user falls below `min_n` and **leans on the baseline** (the gate enforces this
   automatically). Minors-exclusion blocks pooling. Baseline = owner-trained on GPU; flywheel feeds it
   only via consented pooling (+ optional federated nudge, deferred/counsel-gated).
5. **User-as-annotator charter** — integrate the sibling `rally-annotator` (VLC Lua, CSV
   `rally_number,start_time,end_time,ending_reason,sport,shots_count`). Trigger when the gate is
   starved (< min_n) or a corpus threshold is crossed; pick a high-uncertainty ~2-min region
   (LogReg proba ≈ 0.5), guide labeling, ingest CSV as per-user golden labels feeding retune (and,
   with consent, the baseline).
6. **Per-user eval** — `per_user_eval.py`: held-out-USER learning curve (sweep k=1..K, v_old vs v_new
   with `paired_delta_ci` + sign test) = the falsifiable "<5 videos" criterion; a per-user
   no-regression guard (analogous to `regression.py`, against a frozen per-user CONTROL).
7. **Day-0 batteries** — ship the validated label-free Gate-A fusion as the default battery (zero
   per-user labels). Upgrade governance: MINOR (carry per-user model byte-identical) vs MAJOR (re-fit)
   keyed on `feature_schema_hash`.

## Governance
Consent default-deny + enforced at the query (not advisory). **Privacy sequencing:** do NOT advertise
"data never leaves your machine" until on-device ships; near-term pooling carries full cloud posture.
Per-user delete = delete `user_models` + `candidate_segments` for `user_id` (CASCADE already wired).
Roora re-scoped: certify each battery upgrade vs an independent vendor-graded golden set + seed
cold-start (spend does not shrink).

## Phased PR-sized build plan

### Phase 0 — Safety + day-0 batteries (THIS WEEKEND; mostly engineering; no schema/API/served change)
- **PR-0.1 — per-user promotion gate.** ✅ **DONE = PR #141** (`per_user_gate.py` + tests). [engineering]
- **PR-0.2 — held-out-USER learning-curve eval.** `backend/eval/per_user_eval.py` reusing
  `experiment.compare` + `eval_stats.paired_delta_ci`; smallest-k-where-CI-clears-0 logic. [engineering]
- **PR-0.3 — per-user no-regression guard.** per-user CONTROL baseline keyed by `user_id::stage`. [engineering]
- **PR-0.4 — ship Gate-A as the day-0 battery.** Flip `fusion.min_crossings` default + record the
  validated promotion. **[OWNER-GATED — changes shipped default behavior; needs a golden-set regression run.]**
- **PR-0.5 — within-user LOVO measurement harness.** The analysis's "fund this first" experiment to
  confirm/kill the core statistical premise. **[OWNER-GATED — runs on the GPU/WSL box; needs multi-video-per-user data.]**

### Phase 1 — Per-user tuning serving + store
PR-1.1 v4 migration + `set_human_label`/`set_user_id`; PR-1.2 v5 `user_models` + CRUD; PR-1.3
`serving.py` overlay + `load_user_classifier`; **PR-1.4 wire the bridge into `_select_for_handoff`
[OWNER-GATED — served path]**; PR-1.5 `/retune` + `/model` trust feature.

### Phase 2 — Correction loop + flywheel
PR-2.1 `/label` setter; PR-2.2 de-bias prior; PR-2.3 v6 consent ledger + minors-exclusion;
**PR-2.4 opt-in contribution upload [OWNER-GATED — privacy surface].**

### Phase 3 — Annotator charter + taxonomy + baseline upgrades
PR-3.1 active-learning task picker; PR-3.2 rally-annotator CSV ingest → per-user labels;
**PR-3.3 coarse hard/soft shot proxy [OWNER-GATED]**; **PR-3.4 baseline-upgrade governance + federated
nudge [OWNER-GATED, counsel].**

## Honest risks (carried from the analysis)
Small-N per-user eval noise (central; the gate refuses below min_n + falls back); cold-start (day-0
Gate-A battery is the zero-label floor); privacy deferral (near-term pooling = full cloud posture);
compute (VLM personalization out of scope; v1 = cheap LogReg/threshold/cue layer only).

So nothing to deny, ever.

## Q4 — "flipping" explained (and an honest catch)
Today the validated **held-shuttle guard** (Gate-A: a rally needs ≥2 net-crossings, so a player flicking the shuttle between points isn't counted) is **OFF by default** — it only runs if someone explicitly enables the fusion segmenter. **"Flipping to default" = turning that protection ON out-of-the-box for everyone** (the measured win: ΔF1 +0.074, 6/6 matches, p=0.031).

**The catch:** Gate-A lives in the `FusionSegmenter`, which **isn't the default segmenter** (default is `yolo_hybrid`/`gemini`). So "ship it as default" is a real path choice — make that segmenter the default, or port the gate into the default path — and either changes what *every* user gets. **Recommendation:** I run a **golden-set regression** first (confirm Gate-A-as-default doesn't regress the overall pipeline, not just the isolated A/B), bring you the number, *then* you approve the flip. Want me to set that up? (It's a machine-side run on your golden videos.)

## One thing still needs your call
**Structural-guard scope** (the gate's "never auto-disable" list): I recommend **Gate-A only** for now — it's the *proven* structural guard (its value is in failure modes a user's corpus may not yet contain). **Gate-B** (person-occupancy / `min_players`) is more of a tunable precision cue, so I'd leave it *subject* to per-user A/B, not structurally protected. OK to lock **Gate-A-only structural, `min_n=5`**?

## Building now
**PR-0.3 — per-user no-regression guard** (uses your Q1 `user_id::stage` keying): guarantees a per-user retrain or a baseline upgrade can *never* make a user worse than their incumbent — the per-user regression baseline the analysis said was missing. I'll report it + the still-pending Gate-A regression offer when you decide.

### 1021. assistant (2026-06-14T09:36:17.161Z)

# Personalization Plan — a per-user feature on a generalization-first baseline

**Status: DESIGN — owner-adopted (hybrid); Phase-0 engineering landing.** This is the authoritative
plan for the personalization track. The detailed strategy analysis + the full pros/cons that led here
live in the working artifacts `scratch/PERSONALIZATION_PIVOT_ANALYSIS.md` (the decision-grade
counter-case) and `scratch/PERSONALIZATION_FEATURE_DESIGN.md` (the code-grounded design); this doc is
the checked-in summary + decisions + phased build plan. Peer to
[OWNED_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](OWNED_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md),
[EXPERIMENT_HARNESS.md](EXPERIMENT_HARNESS.md), and [MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION_PLAN.md](MULTI_SIGNAL_FUSION_PLAN.md).

## 0. Thesis & strategic rationale (why *hybrid*, not personalization-first)

**Foundation principle (owner):** *"a tool that gets better the more you help it."* Contribution
(data / video / diagnostics / annotation) improves BOTH the user's own model AND the shared baseline;
**payoff scales with contribution.**

A directional pivot — *personalization-first* (ship a baseline that continually self-optimizes to one
user's own footage) — was researched in depth. The verdict was **HYBRID, not all-in**:

- **Adopt personalization as a flag-gated FEATURE on a generalization-first baseline.** The harness
  genuinely makes per-user *tuning* near-free (it is already a corpus-relative A/B engine; a per-user
  corpus is just a special case). This is real and worth shipping.
- **Do NOT bet the strategy on per-user *learning*.** Per-user A/B is the n≈6 small-sample regime
  *worse* (sharding data when you should pool); the differentiated parts (a learned per-user model
  serving path, the correction→label write path, a user/tenant dimension) are largely unbuilt; a
  naively-overfit per-user model loses the cross-user data flywheel and has no shared baseline to
  regress against.
- **The owner's contribution-flywheel + free-tier-pooling closes the one real hole** the counter-case
  found: by having (free-tier) users contribute to the *shared* baseline, the compounding cross-user
  moat is preserved *alongside* personalization — personalization **and** flywheel, not either/or.

Net: a generalization-first **baseline** ("batteries"), a thin **per-user tuning** layer gated by the
honest small-N statistics (with a hard floor + structural-guard protection), and a **contribution
loop** that feeds both.

## 1. Owner decisions (locked 2026-06-14)

1. **Identity** — auth WILL land; *design for the north star (multi-user / cloud), implement for
   current use (single-user local)*. `user_id` nullable now (NULL = local install), device/install
   UUID for the alpha; real auth + a `users` table later.
2. **Per-user model storage** — inline `classifier_json` in the (local) DB now, but **behind a load
   interface** so that post-auth it is fetched from the **cloud-hosted DB run by the service** that
   generates base models and orchestrates the product. The local store is one implementation of that
   interface.
3. **`min_n` is a PROMOTION-confidence floor, NOT a service/segmentation gate.** A brand-new user with
   one video is ALWAYS fully segmented by the baseline batteries — never denied, never "give me more
   videos first." `min_n` only gates whether a *per-user* A/B is trusted enough to OVERRIDE a baseline
   cue default *for that user*; below it (or if the CI / sign test don't clear) → keep the baseline.
   **Training-corpus policy:** *no more than needed, no less than all-if-few* — fit on the
   `smallest_k_with_lift` videos (the held-out-USER learning curve), else ALL available.
4. **"Flip Gate-A to default"** = ship the validated Gate-A held-shuttle guard as the **default
   detection path** (today it lives in the opt-in `FusionSegmenter`, which is not the default
   segmenter). Changes served behavior → **gated on a golden-set regression run + owner OK**; still
   open (see §5).
5. **Flywheel = backend property** (not in-product marketing). A **free tier** is likely and
   **free-tier videos ARE pooled** into the baseline (consent baked into the free terms;
   minors-exclusion still enforced) — the clean value-exchange that feeds the owner-trained base model.
   Paid tiers get stronger privacy / opt-out.

**Pending sub-decision:** structural-guard scope — recommended **Gate-A only** (the proven structural
held-shuttle guard; its value is in failure modes a user's corpus may not yet contain), with **Gate-B**
(person-occupancy / `min_players`) left *subject* to per-user A/B; **`min_n = 5`**. (Awaiting owner
confirmation.)

## 2. Architecture

**Two-layer decoupling (already real).** Detection (GPU, run once): `FusionSegmenter` persists the
**full superset** of per-window features into `candidate_segments.stats`; only the served handoff is
gated. Decision (CPU, swappable): `experiment.Variant` + `predict()` re-score persisted features.
**Personalization == a per-user `Variant`** (cue_flags + `min_crossings`/`min_players` + optional
LogReg + threshold). No segmenter rewrite — a per-user `FusionConfig` overlay resolved upstream.

**The single highest-leverage wiring:** `fusion_hybrid.py::_select_for_handoff` is the production
decision seam. When a per-user model is pinned AND the promotion gate says ON, apply
`LogisticRegression.predict_proba` over `window_stats` (the same math `experiment.predict()` runs
offline). `LogisticRegression.load` is **never called in `backend/pipeline/` today** — the serving
bridge is the #1 wall.

**Per-user data model** (migrations follow the `PRAGMA user_version` ladder; current = v3):
- **v4** — nullable `user_id` on `videos` + `candidate_segments` (NULL = local; byte-identical to today).
- **v5** — `user_models` store: `(user_id, version, baseline_version, feature_schema_hash,
  fusion_config, classifier_json, promotion_evidence, n_videos_at_fit, is_active)`. Inline
  `classifier_json` (tenant-safe); `feature_schema_hash` is the MINOR-vs-MAJOR upgrade switch.
- **v6** — `contribution_consent` ledger (default-deny; minors-exclusion enforced **at the pooling
  query**, not advisory).

## 3. Constructs (the gap list + what is built)

| # | Construct | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Per-user store + serving bridge (wire `LogisticRegression.load` into `_select_for_handoff`) | Phase 1 (the #1 wall) |
| 2 | Correction-loop → per-user labels (`human_label` setter + confirm/reject API; recall-protecting de-bias prior) | Phase 2 (`human_label` is a read-only stub today) |
| 3 | **Per-user promotion gate** (min-N floor + structural-guard exemption) | ✅ **DONE — PR #141** (`backend/eval/per_user_gate.py`) |
| 4 | Contribution flywheel (opt-in data/video/diagnostics → shared baseline; payoff ∝ contribution; consent + minors-exclusion) | Phase 2 |
| 5 | User-as-annotator charter (rally-annotator: auto-generate a ~2-min high-uncertainty segment from the user's own video; guide labeling → grounding) | Phase 3 |
| 6a | **Held-out-USER learning curve** (the falsifiable "<K videos to superior quality" criterion) | ✅ **DONE — PR #142** (`backend/eval/per_user_eval.py`) |
| 6b | Per-user no-regression guard (frozen per-user CONTROL; never accept a regressing retrain/upgrade) | 🔨 **in flight** (`feat/per-user-no-regression`) |
| 7 | Day-0 "batteries" = the validated label-free Gate-A/B fusion (ΔF1 +0.074, 6/6, p=0.031) shipped as the default | Phase 0, owner-gated (§5) |

## 4. Phased PR-sized build plan + status

**Phase 0 — safety + day-0 batteries** (no schema / API / served-behavior change; pure-Python + tests):
- PR-0.1 per-user promotion gate — ✅ **#141 merged**
- PR-0.2 held-out-USER learning curve — ✅ **#142 merged**
- PR-0.3 per-user no-regression guard — 🔨 in flight
- PR-0.4 ship Gate-A as the day-0 battery — **owner-gated** (§5; needs a golden-set regression run)
- PR-0.5 within-user LOVO measurement (the "confirm-or-kill" experiment) — **owner-gated** (needs multi-video-per-user data on the GPU box)

**Phase 1 — per-user tuning serving + store:** v4 migration + `set_human_label`/`set_user_id`; v5
`user_models` + CRUD; `serving.py` overlay resolver + `load_user_classifier`; **wire the bridge into
`_select_for_handoff` (owner-gated — served path)**; `/retune` + `/model` trust-feature endpoints.

**Phase 2 — correction loop + flywheel:** `POST /api/candidates/{id}/label` (the first `human_label`
writer); recall-protecting de-bias prior; v6 consent ledger + minors-exclusion; **opt-in contribution
upload (owner-gated — privacy surface)**; free-tier pooling.

**Phase 3 — annotator charter + taxonomy + baseline upgrades:** active-learning task picker; rally-
annotator CSV ingest → per-user labels; **coarse hard/soft shot proxy (owner-gated)**; **baseline-
upgrade governance (MINOR carry / MAJOR re-fit on `feature_schema_hash`) + optional federated nudge
(owner-gated, counsel).**

## 5. Open decisions (owner)

1. **Structural-guard scope + `min_n` value** — lock **Gate-A-only structural, `min_n = 5`** (recommended)?
2. **Gate-A default flip (PR-0.4)** — Gate-A lives in the non-default `FusionSegmenter`, so "ship as
   default" is a path choice (make that segmenter the default vs port the gate into the default path).
   Recommended sequence: **run a golden-set regression first**, bring the number, *then* approve.
3. **Per-user `user_id` for the alpha** — device/install UUID acceptable, or must auth land first?
4. **Local-install flywheel default** — fully-local zero-pooling until consent is explicitly granted?

## 6. Honest risks (carried from the analysis)

- **Small-N per-user eval noise** is central and *worse* per-user — mitigated structurally: the gate
  refuses below `min_n` and falls back to the baseline; never auto-promotes in the regime the tooling
  exists to refuse in. PR-0.5 confirms-or-kills the core premise before any serving build-out.
- **Cold-start** — the day-0 Gate-A battery (zero per-user labels) is the floor for the median user.
- **Privacy deferral** — do not advertise "data never leaves your machine" until on-device ships;
  near-term pooling carries the full cloud (DPA / consent / minors) posture.
- **Compute** — heavyweight VLM personalization (on-device Qwen3-VL fine-tune) is **out of v1 scope**;
  v1 is the cheap LogReg / threshold / cue-ON-OFF layer only.

## 7. References
- `scratch/PERSONALIZATION_PIVOT_ANALYSIS.md` — the decision-grade strategy analysis (pros/cons, harness-fit, counter-case, recommendation).
- `scratch/PERSONALIZATION_FEATURE_DESIGN.md` — the code-grounded design (schema, serving bridge, APIs, critical files).
- Built: `backend/eval/per_user_gate.py` (#141), `backend/eval/per_user_eval.py` (#142).
- Harness: [EXPERIMENT_HARNESS.md](EXPERIMENT_HARNESS.md), `backend/eval/experiment.py`, `backend/eval/eval_stats.py`.

## Exec summary (~250 words)

The harness already measures a B−A lift honestly — LOVO + bootstrap CI + paired sign test (`experiment.compare` reading from `eval_stats`). **An ablation is just a structured family of those comparisons** where B = the full signal set and each A = "full set MINUS one signal," so the ΔF1 it reports IS that signal's marginal contribution. No new scoring math — the ablation layer is a *driver* over `compare` + `eval_stats` + `segmentation_metrics`, exactly as `compare` was a driver over `metrics`/`calibration`.

A signal = one feature column (or a producer's column group: `shuttle`, `gate_a`, `person`, `audio`, plus future `service_fault`/`warmup`/`shuttle_state`). Ablating it = subtracting its columns from a `Variant`'s `feature_names` (or zeroing `min_crossings` for Gate-A) — no branch, no re-detection. The runner emits a per-signal ΔF1 table (CI + sign test + C4 over-seg). The **Signal-Relevance Ledger** appends each run as a timestamped block so a signal's contribution becomes a time series; a signal trending to ≈0 across K≥3 runs (CI spanning 0, sign-test n.s.) is flagged `STALE_CANDIDATE` — the quantified "is this old signal dead weight?" answer.

Because naive leave-one-out misses redundancy/synergy, the design adds leave-pair-out + greedy backward-elimination (minimal sufficient set) and optional exact Shapley over groups (k≤6, affordable). Small-N honesty is inherited wholesale from `eval_stats` + `per_user_gate`'s bars, including the **structural-guard exemption** (Gate-A never auto-demoted on "no golden lift"). It composes with the leaderboard, `QUALITY_ITERATIONS.md`, and generalizes to per-user ablation via `per_user_gate` in reverse ("motion cue not relevant FOR THIS USER").

---

- **PR-A0 — Signal inventory + `ablation.py` LOSO/LOGO runner.** `Signal` / `AblationConfig` / `AblationReport` + `ablate_one` + `run_ablation`, a pure driver over `experiment.compare` (no new scoring math). Hard-code the current 4-group inventory; `structural` flag on `gate_a`. Unit-tested on synthetic candidate rows (deterministic, GPU-free). **DoD:** reproduces the recorded `QUALITY_ITERATIONS` person/gate_a numbers from a fixture within tolerance.
- **PR-A1 — Results table + leaderboard wiring.** Sorted markdown/ASCII ablation table; append each row to `experiment_leaderboard.json` via `record_experiment`; a `--check-no-regression` mode (math drift guard). CLI: `python -m backend.eval.ablation --manifest output/human_lovo_manifest.json`.

(Later phases — time-series relevance ledger, interaction analysis, per-user ablation — are listed and sequenced in §9, with engineering vs owner-gated marked.)

---

## Top open design questions

1. **Granularity default** — report relevance at producer-GROUP level (LOGO, matches "is this old signal relevant") or column level (LOSO, catches a dead column inside a useful group), or always both?
2. **Dead-weight trend rule** — are K≥3 consecutive washes / |rolling Δ|&lt;ε / sign-never-significant the right knobs, and should the flag require n non-decreasing across the K runs so corpus shrinkage can't fake staleness?
3. **Re-measure cadence** — re-run the ledger on EVERY harness run (auto) or a separate explicit `make ablate` cadence (per merged cue + periodic)?
4. **Shapley scope** — exact Shapley over ≤6 groups is affordable; worth adding now for paper-grade fair credit, or defer until the corpus is large enough that its small-N uncertainty isn't the dominant caveat?
5. **Multiplicity correction** — apply Holm/BH across the k simultaneous ablation tests now (more honest, may mask a real signal at n=6) or report raw p with a family-wise caveat until k grows?
6. **Per-user trigger** — do enough users clear `min_n` videos, and is per-user signal-*retirement* desired at all, or should personalization stay add-only for safety?

The **base choice** is settled and already wired: a **frozen WASB shuttle substrate (MIT)** + a single-sourced featurizer (`backend/features/rally_seq.py`, train==serve, schema-versioned) + an **owned lightweight temporal head** (LogReg → ActionFormer/ASFormer, all MIT). ### 1135. assistant (2026-06-14T13:27:06.597Z)

(Decoded past the cat-on-keyboard 🐱⌨️ — there's a real, repeated question in there, so let me take it seriously.)

This is a legitimate criminology question, and the right way to honor your "only government data, no SEO junk, agree-or-refute" rule is to test it against what India's official statistics actually contain. Done honestly, **the data refutes the hypothesis — but mostly by refuting its *testability*, and the one piece that is measurable means something almost opposite to what it looks like.** Three layers:

## 1. The specific predictors you named are not recorded in *any* Indian government crime dataset
India's only authoritative crime data is **NCRB's *Crime in India* and *Prison Statistics India***. *Prison Statistics* records an inmate's **education *level*** — illiterate / below class X / class X–to–below-graduate / graduate / postgraduate / technical. It does **not** record **school *type*** (government vs private), **board** (State vs CBSE/ICSE), or **individual exam marks**. No government instrument links any of those to criminality.

→ So two of your three legs — **board** and **marks** — are **unfalsifiable with authorized data**; there is literally nothing to test them against. The public-vs-private leg, likewise, isn't in the data. A hypothesis you can't falsify isn't confirmed; it's unscientific *as posed*.

## 2. The one adjacent thing that *is* measured (prisoner education level) cannot carry the inference
The prison-education distribution does skew toward less education — but that number can't mean "less-educated people are more criminal," for three reasons that are themselves data-grounded:

- **Prison ≠ criminal population.** It measures who is *arrested, charged, convicted, and unable to post bail*. In India **~3 of 4 prisoners are undertrials** (not convicted). It's the criminal-justice *funnel*, shaped by who can afford a lawyer and bail — not a census of offenders.
- **Confounding by class.** Government school + State board + low marks are all **markers of lower socioeconomic status**, which independently predicts arrest/incarceration through differential policing, weaker legal defense, and bail unaffordability. The correlation is largely a **class-selection artifact of the justice system**, not a property of the schooling.
- **Ecological fallacy + reverse causation** — group rates don't speak to individuals, and incarceration itself truncates education.

## 3. What the rigorous (peer-reviewed) literature says
Where *causal* designs exist, more schooling tends to **reduce** offending — but that's about education *quantity*, not school type/board/marks, and it's confounded everywhere; none of it resolves your specific variables for India.

## Verdict
**Refuted, on the data's own terms.** Two of the three claims have *no* measurable government data; the third (education level of prisoners) reflects **the carceral system's selection of the poor**, which is a statement about policing and poverty — not about who commits crime, and not an indictment of government-schooled students. The honest reading flips your prior: the prison-education skew is evidence that *poverty gets caught*, not that *low marks cause crime*.

If you want the **receipts** — the exact *Prison Statistics India* education tables (latest year + the multi-year trend), the precise undertrial share, and the peer-reviewed India criminology — say the word and I'll pull a fully NCRB/MoSPI-sourced report with zero SEO citations. (It still won't contain school-type or board — because the state simply doesn't collect it.)

Now back to your rain. ☔
